sentences.zh: 藝術夫陰陽所以正時日，順氣序者也；

translations.literal: As for the arts, yin-yang studies serve to correct the calendar and day-count and to align with the sequence of qi.
translations.idiomatic: The arts of yin-yang exist to set the calendar aright and keep human activity in step with the seasons.

sentences.zh: 卜筮所以決嫌疑，定猶豫者也；

translations.literal: Divination by tortoise shell and milfoil serves to resolve doubts and suspicions and to settle hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Divination exists to cut through doubt and settle what reason alone cannot decide.

sentences.zh: 醫巫所以禦妖邪，養性命者也；

translations.literal: Medicine and shamanism serve to ward off evil spirits and to nurture life and vital essence.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine and ritual healing serve to repel malign forces and preserve life.

sentences.zh: 音律所以和人神，節哀樂者也；

translations.literal: Music and pitch standards serve to harmonize humans and spirits and to regulate grief and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Music harmonizes heaven and humanity and gives proper measure to sorrow and celebration.

sentences.zh: 相術所以辯貴賤，明分理者也；

translations.literal: Physiognomy serves to distinguish noble and base and to clarify proper distinctions and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Physiognomy distinguishes rank and fortune and clarifies the lines fate draws among men.

sentences.zh: 技巧所以利器用，濟艱難者也。

translations.literal: Technical skill serves to improve instruments and tools and to overcome hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Technical ingenuity refines tools and sees people through hard times.

sentences.zh: 此皆聖人無心，因民設教，救恤災患，禁止淫邪。

translations.literal: All these were undertaken by the sages without self-interest, setting up teachings according to the people's needs, relieving and succoring in disaster and calamity, and forbidding excess and depravity.
translations.idiomatic: The sages pursued none of these for personal gain; they shaped them as public teachings to relieve suffering in disaster and to check excess and evil.

sentences.zh: 自三五哲王，其所由來久矣。

translations.literal: Since the wise kings of the Three and Five Emperors, their origins have been long-established.
translations.idiomatic: Their roots reach back to the sage rulers of antiquity and stretch across the ages.

sentences.zh: 然昔之言陰陽者，則有箕子、裨灶、梓慎、子韋；

translations.literal: Yet among those who spoke of yin-yang in former times were Jizi, Pi Zao, Zi Shen, and Zi Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Masters of yin-yang in antiquity include Jizi, Pi Zao, Zi Shen, and Zi Wei;

sentences.zh: 曉音律者，則師曠、師摯、伯牙、杜夔；

translations.literal: Those versed in music and pitch were Shi Kuang, Shi Zhi, Boya, and Du Kui;
translations.idiomatic: Masters of music include Shi Kuang, Shi Zhi, Boya, and Du Kui;

sentences.zh: 敘卜筮，則史扁、史蘇、嚴君平、司馬季主；

translations.literal: In recounting divination, there were Shi Bian, Shi Su, Yan Junping, and Sima Jizhu;
translations.idiomatic: In divination, there were Shi Bian, Shi Su, Yan Junping, and Sima Jizhu;

sentences.zh: 論相術，則內史叔服、姑布子卿、唐舉、許負；

translations.literal: In discussing physiognomy, there were Inner Scribe Shufu, Gubu Ziqing, Tang Ju, and Xu Fu;
translations.idiomatic: In physiognomy, there were Inner Scribe Shufu, Gubu Ziqing, Tang Ju, and Xu Fu;

sentences.zh: 語醫，則文摯、扁鵲、季咸、華佗；

translations.literal: In speaking of medicine, there were Wen Zhi, Bian Que, Ji Xian, and Hua Tuo;
translations.idiomatic: In medicine, there were Wen Zhi, Bian Que, Ji Xian, and Hua Tuo;

sentences.zh: 其巧思，則奚仲、墨翟、張平子、馬德衡。

translations.literal: In ingenious craft, there were Xi Zhong, Mo Di, Zhang Heng, and Ma Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In ingenious craft, there were Xi Zhong, Mo Di, Zhang Heng, and Ma Jun.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸君者，仰觀俯察，探賾索隱，鹹詣幽微，思侔造化，通靈入妙，殊才絕技。

translations.literal: All these gentlemen looked up to observe the heavens and looked down to examine the earth, probing the profound and searching out the hidden, all attaining the subtle and recondite; their thought matched creation itself, penetrating the numinous and entering the marvelous—their talents extraordinary and their skills unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: These men read heaven above and earth below, probing what is hidden and reaching into the subtle. Their minds rivaled creation itself; their insight touched the numinous. Each possessed rare genius and supreme mastery.

sentences.zh: 或弘道以濟時，或隱身以利物，深不可測，固無得而稱焉。

translations.literal: Some spread the Way to aid their age; some hid themselves yet benefited others. Their depths cannot be fathomed—truly there is no way to do them full justice in words.
translations.idiomatic: Some brought the Way into the world to save their times; others withdrew from sight yet still served others. Their depths cannot be measured, and no praise can do them justice.

sentences.zh: 近古涉乎斯術者，鮮有存夫貞一，多肆其淫僻，厚誣天道。

translations.literal: In more recent times those who practiced these arts have rarely preserved steadfast integrity; most indulged depraved eccentricities and gravely misrepresented the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, few who pursued these arts kept to a single-minded integrity. Most gave free rein to perverse practices and grossly abused the name of Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 或變亂陰陽，曲成君欲，或假託神怪，熒惑民心。

translations.literal: Some distorted yin and yang to contrive what their lords desired; some feigned divine portents and spirits to bewilder the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Some twisted the laws of yin and yang to gratify a ruler's desires; others used false omens and marvels to mislead the people.

sentences.zh: 遂令時俗妖訛，不獲返其真性，身罹災毒，莫得壽終而死。

translations.literal: Thus the customs of the age turned grotesque and corrupt, people could not return to their true natures, bodies suffered calamity and poison, and none could live out their years and die a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: Custom grew grotesque and corrupt; people lost their true natures, fell prey to disaster, and died before their time.

sentences.zh: 藝成而下，意在茲乎？

translations.literal: "When the arts have reached completion, they decline"—is that the meaning intended here?
translations.idiomatic: When an art has reached its height, it declines—is that what this means?

sentences.zh: 曆觀經史百家之言，無不存夫藝術，或敘其玄妙，或記其迂誕，非徒用廣異聞，將以明乎勸戒。

translations.literal: Surveying the sayings of the classics, histories, and the hundred schools, all contain records of these arts—some narrating their mysteries, some recording their absurdities—not merely to broaden strange hearsay, but to make clear warnings and admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: Read through the classics, histories, and all schools of learning and you find the arts everywhere recorded—some telling of their wonders, some of their absurdities—not merely to entertain with marvels, but to teach by warning.

sentences.zh: 是以後來作者，或相祖述，故今亦采其尤著者，列為《藝術篇》雲。

translations.literal: Therefore later writers have often followed and transmitted one another's accounts; hence I now also select the most notable cases and arrange them in the "Treatise on the Arts."
translations.idiomatic: Later writers have followed one another in recording such stories, and so I have gathered the most notable among them into this "Treatise on the Arts."

sentences.zh: 庾季才子質盧太翼耿詢

translations.literal: Yu Jicai, Zi Zhi, Lu Taiyi, Geng Xun
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jicai, Zi Zhi, Lu Taiyi, and Geng Xun

sentences.zh: 庾季才，字叔奕，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Jicai, courtesy name Shuyi, was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jicai, styled Shuyi, came from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 八世祖滔，隨晉元帝過江，官至散騎常侍，封遂昌侯，因家于南郡江陵縣。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Tao followed Emperor Yuan of Jin across the Yangtze, reached the office of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Suichang, and the family settled in Jiangling County, Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations back his ancestor Yu Tao crossed the Yangtze with Emperor Yuan of Jin, rose to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, received the title Marquis of Suichang, and settled the family in Jiangling, Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖詵，梁處士，與宗人易齊名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shen was a reclusive scholar of Liang, famed alongside his clansman Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shen was a Liang recluse who shared renown with his kinsman Yi.

sentences.zh: 父曼倩，光祿卿。

translations.literal: His father Manqian was Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Manqian served as Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 季才幼穎悟，八歲誦《尚書》，十二通《周易》，好占玄象。

translations.literal: Jicai was bright and quick as a child; at eight he could recite the Documents, at twelve he mastered the Changes, and he loved to prognosticate from celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai was precocious: at eight he could recite the Documents, at twelve he had mastered the Changes, and he took to reading the heavens.

sentences.zh: 居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: While in mourning he was known for his filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial devotion during his period of mourning.

sentences.zh: 梁廬陵王績辟荊州主簿，湘東王繹重其術藝，引授外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Ji of Luling of Liang recruited him as Registrar of Jing Province; Prince Yi of Xiangdong valued his arts and appointed him External Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Luling recruited him as Registrar of Jing Province; Prince Yi of Xiangdong, impressed by his skills, made him External Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 西台建，累遷中書郎，領太史，封宜昌縣伯。

translations.literal: When the Western Headquarters was established, he was promoted repeatedly to Palace Gentleman and concurrently served as Grand Astrologer, enfeoffed as Baron of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Headquarters was established, he rose through the ranks to Palace Gentleman, concurrently served as Grand Astrologer, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 季才固辭太史，元帝曰：「漢司馬遷曆世屍掌，魏高堂隆猶領此職，不無前例，卿何憚焉。」

translations.literal: Jicai firmly declined the post of Grand Astrologer. Emperor Yuan said, "In Han, Sima Qian held this office generation after generation; in Wei, Gao Tanglong still held it—there is precedent. Why do you shrink from it?"
translations.idiomatic: Jicai firmly declined the post of Grand Astrologer. Emperor Yuan said, "In Han, Sima Qian held this office generation after generation; in Wei, Gao Tanglong still held it—there is precedent. Why do you shrink from it?"

sentences.zh: 帝亦頗明星曆，因共仰觀，從容謂季才曰：「朕猶慮禍起蕭牆，何方可息？」

translations.literal: The emperor was also fairly versed in astronomy and the calendar; they therefore observed the heavens together, and at leisure the emperor said to Jicai, "I still worry that trouble will rise within the palace walls—what means can quell it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was also fairly versed in astronomy and the calendar; they therefore observed the heavens together, and at leisure the emperor said to Jicai, "I still worry that trouble will rise within the palace walls—what means can quell it?"

sentences.zh: 季才曰：「頃天象告變，秦將入郢，陛下宜留重臣，作鎮荊陝，整旆還都，以避其患。

translations.literal: Jicai said, "Recently the heavens have shown signs of change: Qin forces will enter Ying. Your Majesty should leave senior ministers behind to guard Jing and Shaan, marshal your banners, and return to the capital to avoid the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai said, "Recently the heavens have shown signs of change: Qin forces will enter Ying. Your Majesty should leave senior ministers behind to guard Jing and Shaan, marshal your banners, and return to the capital to avoid the calamity.

sentences.zh: 假令羯寇侵蹙，止失荊湘，在於社稷，可得無慮。

translations.literal: Even if the Jie invaders press hard, you would lose only Jing and Xiang; as for the altars of state, there need be no concern.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Jie invaders press hard, you would lose only Jing and Xiang; the altars of state themselves need not be at risk.

sentences.zh: 必久停留，恐非天意也。」

translations.literal: If you stay long, I fear that will not accord with Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: If you stay long, I fear that will not accord with Heaven's intent."

sentences.zh: 帝初然之，後與吏部尚書宗懍等議，乃止。

translations.literal: At first the emperor agreed, but after discussing the matter with Minister of Personnel Zong Jin and others, he dropped the plan.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor agreed, but after discussing the matter with Minister of Personnel Zong Jin and others, he dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 俄而江陵陷滅，竟如其言。

translations.literal: Before long Jiangling fell and was destroyed, exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jiangling fell and was destroyed, exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 周太祖一見季才，深加優禮，令參掌太史。

translations.literal: At their first meeting, Emperor Taizu of Zhou treated Jicai with exceptional courtesy and had him assist in managing the Grand Astrologer's office.
translations.idiomatic: At their first meeting, Emperor Taizu of Zhou treated Jicai with exceptional courtesy and had him assist in managing the Grand Astrologer's office.

sentences.zh: 每有征討，恆預侍從。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a campaign, he was always present in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was a campaign, he was always present in attendance.

sentences.zh: 賜宅一區，水田十頃，並奴婢牛羊什物等，謂季才曰：「卿是南人，未安北土，故有此賜者，欲絕卿南望之心。

translations.literal: He was granted one residence, ten qing of irrigated fields, and slaves, servants, cattle, sheep, and other goods, and the emperor said to Jicai, "You are a man of the south and are not yet settled in the northern lands; this grant is meant to cut off your longing to look south.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one residence, ten qing of irrigated fields, and slaves, servants, cattle, sheep, and other goods, and the emperor said to Jicai, "You are a man of the south and are not yet settled in the northern lands; this grant is meant to cut off your longing to look south.

sentences.zh: 宜盡誠事我，當以富貴相答。」

translations.literal: Serve me with full loyalty, and I shall repay you with wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Serve me with full loyalty, and I shall repay you with wealth and honor."

sentences.zh: 初，郢都之陷也，衣冠士人多沒為賤。

translations.literal: When Ying fell at first, many gentry and officials were reduced to servitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying fell at first, many gentry and officials were reduced to servitude.

sentences.zh: 季才散所賜物，購求親故。

translations.literal: Jicai distributed what he had been granted to purchase and redeem relatives and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai distributed what he had been granted to purchase and redeem relatives and old friends.

sentences.zh: 文帝問：「何能若此？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen asked, "How can you do this?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen asked, "How can you do this?"

sentences.zh: 季才曰：「僕聞魏克襄陽，先昭異度，晉平建業，喜得士衡。

translations.literal: Jicai said, "I have heard that when Wei took Xiangyang, they first sought out Yi Du; when Jin pacified Jianye, they rejoiced to gain Lu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai said, "I have heard that when Wei took Xiangyang, they first sought out Yi Du; when Jin pacified Jianye, they rejoiced to gain Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 伐國求賢，古之道也。

translations.literal: In conquering a state, one seeks out the worthy—such is the ancient Way.
translations.idiomatic: In conquering a state, one seeks out the worthy—such is the ancient Way.

sentences.zh: 今郢都覆敗，君信有罪，晉紳何咎，皆為賤隸！

translations.literal: Now Ying has been overthrown; if the lord was guilty, what crime did the gentry commit, that all should become base slaves!
translations.idiomatic: Now Ying has been overthrown; if the lord was guilty, what crime did the gentry commit, that all should become base slaves!

sentences.zh: 鄙人羈旅，不敢獻言，誠切哀之，故贖購耳。」

translations.literal: I am but a man stranded far from home and dare not speak up; I was moved only by pity, and so I redeemed them."
translations.idiomatic: I am but a man stranded far from home and dare not speak up; I was moved only by pity, and so I redeemed them."

sentences.zh: 太祖乃悟曰：「吾之過也。

translations.literal: Taizu then understood and said, "This was my fault.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then understood and said, "This was my fault.

sentences.zh: 微君遂失天下之望！」

translations.literal: But for you, I would have lost the hope of the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: But for you, I would have lost the hope of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 因出令免梁俘為奴婢者數千口。

translations.literal: He then issued an order freeing several thousand Liang captives who had been made slaves and servants.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an order freeing several thousand Liang captives who had been made slaves and servants.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，與王褒、庾信同補麟趾學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng, he was appointed together with Wang Bao and Yu Xin as a Linqi Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wucheng, he was appointed together with Wang Bao and Yu Xin as a Linqi Academician.

sentences.zh: 累遷稍伯大夫、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Grand Master of the Palace, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Senior Grand Master of State with the Three Excellencies' Honors.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to Grand Master of the Palace, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Senior Grand Master of State with the Three Excellencies' Honors.

sentences.zh: 其後大塚宰宇文護執政，謂季才曰：「比日天道，有何徵祥？」

translations.literal: Later, when Grand Minister Yuwen Hu held power, he said to Jicai, "Of late, what omens has Heaven shown?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Grand Minister Yuwen Hu held power, he said to Jicai, "Of late, what omens has Heaven shown?"

sentences.zh: 季才對曰：「荷恩深厚，若不盡言，便同木石。

translations.literal: Jicai replied, "Your grace has shown me deep favor; if I do not speak fully, I am no better than wood or stone.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai replied, "Your grace has shown me deep favor; if I do not speak fully, I am no better than wood or stone.

sentences.zh: 頃上臺有變，不利宰輔，公宜歸政天子，請老私門。

translations.literal: Recently there has been a change in the upper palace—a sign unfavorable to the chief minister. My lord should return power to the Son of Heaven and request retirement in his private home.
translations.idiomatic: Recently there has been a change in the upper palace—a sign unfavorable to the chief minister. My lord should return power to the Son of Heaven and request retirement in his private home.

sentences.zh: 此則自享期頤，而受旦、奭之美，子孫籓屏，終保維城之固。

translations.literal: Then you yourself will enjoy a full span of years and receive the glory of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao; your descendants will serve as bulwarks of the realm and forever preserve the strength of the outer walls.
translations.idiomatic: Then you yourself will enjoy a full span of years and receive the glory of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao; your descendants will serve as bulwarks of the realm and forever preserve the strength of the outer walls.

sentences.zh: 不然者，非複所知。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, what follows is beyond my knowledge."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, what follows is beyond my knowledge."

sentences.zh: 護沈吟久之，謂季才曰：「吾本意如此，但辭未獲免耳。

translations.literal: Hu pondered a long while, then said to Jicai, "That was my original intent, but my resignation was never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Hu pondered a long while, then said to Jicai, "That was my original intent, but my resignation was never accepted.

sentences.zh: 公既王官，可依朝例，無煩別參寡人也。」

translations.literal: Since you hold a royal office, follow court routine; there is no need to come separately to see me."
translations.idiomatic: Since you hold a royal office, follow court routine; there is no need to come separately to see me."

sentences.zh: 自是漸疏，不復別見。

translations.literal: From then on he gradually kept his distance and no longer received separate audiences.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he gradually kept his distance and no longer received separate audiences.

sentences.zh: 及護滅之後，閱其書記，武帝親自臨檢，有假託符命，妄造異端者，皆致誅戮。

translations.literal: After Hu was destroyed, when his papers were examined, Emperor Wu personally inspected them; those who had forged mandates of fate and invented heterodox doctrines were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu was destroyed, when his papers were examined, Emperor Wu personally inspected them; those who had forged mandates of fate and invented heterodox doctrines were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 唯得季才書兩紙，盛言緯候災祥，宜反政歸權。

translations.literal: Only two letters from Jicai were found, strongly urging that the weft texts and celestial signs showed disaster and auspice and that power should be returned to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Only two letters from Jicai were found, strongly urging that the weft texts and celestial signs showed disaster and auspice and that power should be returned to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝謂少宗伯斛斯徵曰：「庾季才至誠謹愨，甚得人臣之禮。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Husi Zheng, "Yu Jicai is utterly sincere, careful, and upright—truly he observes the rites proper to a minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Husi Zheng, "Yu Jicai is utterly sincere, careful, and upright—truly he observes the rites proper to a minister."

sentences.zh: 因賜粟三百石，帛二百段。

translations.literal: He therefore granted three hundred shi of grain and two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore granted three hundred shi of grain and two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遷太史中大夫，詔撰《靈台秘苑》，加上儀同，封臨潁伯，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: Jicai was promoted to Grand Master of the Astrologer's Office; an edict ordered him to compile the Secret Garden of the Spirit Terrace, and he was given the added honor of Senior Grand Master of State, enfeoffed as Baron of Linying with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai was promoted to Grand Master of the Astrologer's Office; an edict ordered him to compile the Secret Garden of the Spirit Terrace, and he was given the added honor of Senior Grand Master of State, enfeoffed as Baron of Linying with a fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Jicai was given the additional titles of General of Agile Cavalry and Senior Grand Master of State with the Opening of an Office, and his fief was increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Jicai was given the additional titles of General of Agile Cavalry and Senior Grand Master of State with the Opening of an Office, and his fief was increased by three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，嘗夜召季才而問曰：「吾以庸虛，受茲顧命，天時人事，卿以為何如？」

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, he once summoned Jicai at night and asked, "I have received this charge in my mediocrity and inadequacy—what do you make of the signs of Heaven and the affairs of men?"
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became Chancellor, he once summoned Jicai at night and asked, "I have received this charge in my mediocrity and inadequacy—what do you make of the signs of Heaven and the affairs of men?"

sentences.zh: 季才曰：「天道精微，難可意察，切以人事卜之，符兆已定。

translations.literal: Jicai said, "The Way of Heaven is subtle and hard to grasp by mere intent; judged strictly by human affairs, the omen is already fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai said, "The Way of Heaven is subtle and hard to grasp by mere intent; judged strictly by human affairs, the omen is already fixed.

sentences.zh: 季才縱言不可，公豈複得為箕、潁之事乎？」

translations.literal: Even if Jicai said it could not be done, would you, my lord, still be able to retire to the life of Ji and Ying?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if Jicai said it could not be done, would you, my lord, still be able to retire to the life of Ji and Ying?"

sentences.zh: 高祖默然久之，因舉首曰：「吾今譬猶騎獸，誠不得下矣。」

translations.literal: Gaozu was silent a long while, then raised his head and said, "I am now like a man riding a beast—I truly cannot dismount."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was silent a long while, then raised his head and said, "I am now like a man riding a beast—I truly cannot dismount."

sentences.zh: 因賜雜彩五十匹，絹二百段，曰：「愧公此意，宜善為思之。」

translations.literal: He then granted fifty bolts of patterned silk and two hundred bolts of plain silk, saying, "I am ashamed before your intent; think carefully on this."
translations.idiomatic: He then granted fifty bolts of patterned silk and two hundred bolts of plain silk, saying, "I am ashamed before your intent; think carefully on this."

sentences.zh: 大定元年正月，季才言曰：「今月戊戌平旦，青氣如樓闕，見於國城之上，俄而變紫，逆風西行。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Dading, Jicai said, "On the day wuxu of this month at dawn, green qi like a tower-gate appeared above the capital; soon it turned purple and moved west against the wind.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Dading, Jicai said, "On the day wuxu of this month at dawn, green qi like a tower-gate appeared above the capital; soon it turned purple and moved west against the wind.

sentences.zh: 《氣經》雲：『天不能無雲而雨，皇王不能無氣而立。』

translations.literal: The Classic of Qi says, 'Heaven cannot be without clouds and yet send rain; a king cannot be without qi and yet stand firm.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Qi says, 'Heaven cannot be without clouds and yet send rain; a king cannot be without qi and yet stand firm.'

sentences.zh: 今王氣已見，須即應之。

translations.literal: Now the kingly qi has appeared; you must respond to it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Now the kingly qi has appeared; you must respond to it at once.

sentences.zh: 二月日出卯入酉，居天之正位，謂之二八之門。

translations.literal: In the second month the sun rises at mao and sets at you, occupying the central position of Heaven—this is called the Gate of Two Eights.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the sun rises at mao and sets at you, occupying the central position of Heaven—this is called the Gate of Two Eights.

sentences.zh: 日者，人君之象，人君正位，宜用二月。

translations.literal: The sun is the image of the ruler; when the ruler occupies the correct position, the second month should be used.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is the image of the ruler; when the ruler occupies the correct position, the second month should be used.

sentences.zh: 其月十三日甲子，甲為六甲之始，子為十二辰之初，甲數九，子數又九，九為天數。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of that month, jiazi, jia is the beginning of the six jia and zi the beginning of the twelve branches; jia counts as nine and zi also counts as nine—nine is Heaven's number.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of that month, jiazi, jia is the beginning of the six jia and zi the beginning of the twelve branches; jia counts as nine and zi also counts as nine—nine is Heaven's number.

sentences.zh: 其日即是驚蟄，陽氣壯發之時。

translations.literal: That day is also the Awakening of Insects, when yang qi surges forth vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: That day is also the Awakening of Insects, when yang qi surges forth vigorously.

sentences.zh: 昔周武王以二月甲子定天下，享年八百，漢高帝以二月甲午即帝位，享年四百，故知甲子、甲午為得天數。

translations.literal: Formerly King Wu of Zhou on jiazi of the second month settled the realm and enjoyed eight hundred years; Emperor Gaozu of Han on jiawu of the second month took the throne and enjoyed four hundred years—thus one knows that jiazi and jiawu accord with Heaven's number.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly King Wu of Zhou on jiazi of the second month settled the realm and enjoyed eight hundred years; Emperor Gaozu of Han on jiawu of the second month took the throne and enjoyed four hundred years—thus one knows that jiazi and jiawu accord with Heaven's number.

sentences.zh: 今二月甲子，宜應天受命。」

translations.literal: On jiazi of the second month now, you should accept Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi of the second month now, you should accept Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，授通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was appointed Regular Attendant in Direct Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was appointed Regular Attendant in Direct Service.

sentences.zh: 高祖將遷都，夜與高熲、蘇威二人定議，季才旦而奏曰：「臣仰觀玄象，俯察圖記，龜兆允襲，必有遷都。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was about to move the capital, he settled the plan at night with Gao Jiong and Su Wei; the next morning Jicai memorialized, "Your servant, looking up to observe the dark signs and looking down to examine charts and records, finds that tortoise and milfoil omens all agree—there must be a move of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was about to move the capital, he settled the plan at night with Gao Jiong and Su Wei; the next morning Jicai memorialized, "Your servant, looking up to observe the dark signs and looking down to examine charts and records, finds that tortoise and milfoil omens all agree—there must be a move of the capital.

sentences.zh: 且堯都平陽，舜都冀土，是知帝王居止，世代不同。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yao made his capital at Pingyang and Shun at Jizhou—thus one knows that where emperors and kings dwell differs from age to age.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yao made his capital at Pingyang and Shun at Jizhou—thus one knows that where emperors and kings dwell differs from age to age.

sentences.zh: 且漢營此城，經今將八百歲，水皆鹹鹵，不甚宜人。

translations.literal: Moreover, Han built this city; nearly eight hundred years have passed, and the water is all brackish and bitter—not very suitable for human habitation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Han built this city; nearly eight hundred years have passed, and the water is all brackish and bitter—not very suitable for human habitation.

sentences.zh: 願陛下協天人之心，為遷徙之計。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will harmonize the hearts of Heaven and man and plan the move."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will harmonize the hearts of Heaven and man and plan the move."

sentences.zh: 高祖愕然，謂熲等曰：「是何神也！」

translations.literal: Gaozu was startled and said to Jiong and the others, "What kind of spirit is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was startled and said to Jiong and the others, "What kind of spirit is this!"

sentences.zh: 遂發詔施行，購絹三百段，馬兩匹，進爵為公。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued to carry it out; he was rewarded with three hundred bolts of silk and two horses, and his rank was advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued to carry it out; he was rewarded with three hundred bolts of silk and two horses, and his rank was advanced to Duke.

sentences.zh: 謂季才曰：「朕自今已後，信有天道矣。」

translations.literal: He said to Jicai, "From now on I shall believe that Heaven has a Way."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Jicai, "From now on I shall believe that Heaven has a Way."

sentences.zh: 於是令季才與其子質撰《垂象》、《地形》等志。

translations.literal: He then ordered Jicai and his son Zhi to compile treatises such as Hanging Images and Topography.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Jicai and his son Zhi to compile treatises such as Hanging Images and Topography.

sentences.zh: 上謂季才曰：「天地秘奧，推測多途，執見不同，或致差舛。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Jicai, "The secrets of Heaven and Earth are profound; there are many paths of inference, and fixed opinions that differ can lead to error.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Jicai, "The secrets of Heaven and Earth are profound; there are many paths of inference, and fixed opinions that differ can lead to error.

sentences.zh: 朕不欲外人干預此事，故使公父子共為之也。」

translations.literal: I do not wish outsiders to interfere in this matter, and so I have you, father and son, undertake it together."
translations.idiomatic: I do not wish outsiders to interfere in this matter, and so I have you, father and son, undertake it together."

sentences.zh: 及書成奏之，賜米千石，絹六百段。

translations.literal: When the work was completed and submitted, he was granted a thousand shi of rice and six hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was completed and submitted, he was granted a thousand shi of rice and six hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 九年，出為均州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was sent out as Governor of Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was sent out as Governor of Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 策書始降，將就籓，時議以季才術藝精通，有詔還委舊任。

translations.literal: When the appointment edict had just been issued and he was about to take up his post as a frontier lord, court opinion held that Jicai's arts were supremely refined, and an edict recalled him to his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment edict had just been issued and he was about to take up his post as a frontier lord, court opinion held that Jicai's arts were supremely refined, and an edict recalled him to his former duties.

sentences.zh: 季才以年老，頻表去職，每降優旨不許。

translations.literal: Jicai, being old, repeatedly memorialized to leave office, but each time a gracious edict refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai, being old, repeatedly memorialized to leave office, but each time a gracious edict refused permission.

sentences.zh: 會張胄玄曆行，及袁充言日影長。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar was put into use, and Yuan Chong spoke of the lengthening of the sun's shadow.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar was put into use, and Yuan Chong spoke of the lengthening of the sun's shadow.

sentences.zh: 上以問季才，季才因言充謬。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Jicai about it, and Jicai declared that Chong was in error.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Jicai about it, and Jicai declared that Chong was in error.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，由是免職，給半祿歸第。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and on that account dismissed him from office, granting half salary and ordering him to return to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, stripped him of office, and sent him home on half pay.

sentences.zh: 所有祥異，常使人就家訪焉。

translations.literal: Whenever there were auspicious or anomalous signs, he regularly sent someone to his home to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever omens appeared, the court still sent messengers to his house to consult him.

sentences.zh: 仁壽三年卒，時年八十八。

translations.literal: In the third year of Renshou he died, at the age of eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Renshou, aged eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 季才局量寬弘，術業優博，篤于信義，志好賓遊。

translations.literal: Jicai was broad-minded and magnanimous, his arts and learning abundant and wide; he was devoted to faith and righteousness and loved to entertain guests.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai was open-hearted and learned, steadfast in loyalty, and fond of gathering friends for conversation.

sentences.zh: 常吉日良辰，與琅琊王褒、彭城劉㲄、河東裴政及宗人信等，為文酒之會。

translations.literal: On auspicious days and fine seasons he would join Wang Bao of Langya, Liu Yan of Pengcheng, Pei Zheng of Hedong, and his clansman Xin in literary and wine gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: On fine days he would meet Wang Bao of Langya, Liu Yan of Pengcheng, Pei Zheng of Hedong, and his kinsman Xin for literary gatherings over wine.

sentences.zh: 次有劉臻、明克讓、柳抃之徒，雖為後進，亦申遊款。

translations.literal: Next came Liu Zhen, Ming Kerang, Liu Bian, and others; though they were juniors, they too were admitted to his company.
translations.idiomatic: After them came Liu Zhen, Ming Kerang, Liu Bian, and others—juniors, but welcome in his circle nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 撰《靈台秘苑》一百二十卷，《垂象志》一百四十二卷，《地形志》八十七卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled the Secret Garden of the Spirit Terrace in one hundred and twenty scrolls, Records of Hanging Images in one hundred and forty-two scrolls, and Records of Topography in eighty-seven scrolls—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Secret Garden of the Spirit Terrace in 120 scrolls, Records of Hanging Images in 142 scrolls, and Records of Topography in 87 scrolls, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 瘐質，字行修，少而明敏，早有志尚。

translations.literal: Yu Zhi, courtesy name Xingxiu, was bright and quick from youth and early showed high ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhi, styled Xingxiu, was clever as a boy and early showed strong purpose.

sentences.zh: 八歲誦梁世祖《玄覽》、《言志》等十賦，拜童子郎。

translations.literal: At eight he could recite ten fu by Emperor Shizu of Liang, including "Dark Contemplation" and "Declaring Intent," and was appointed Attendant Boy.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could recite ten fu by Emperor Shizu of Liang, including "Dark Contemplation" and "Declaring Intent," and was made Attendant Boy.

sentences.zh: 仕周齊煬王記室。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as Recorder to Prince Yang of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he served as Recorder to Prince Yang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，除奉朝請，曆鄢陵令，遷隴州司馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was appointed Attendant at Court; he served as Magistrate of Yanling and was promoted to Administrator of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he became Attendant at Court, later served as Magistrate of Yanling, and was promoted to Administrator of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大業初，授太史令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daye era he was appointed Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 操履貞愨，立言忠鯁，每有災異，必指事面陳。

translations.literal: His conduct was upright and sincere; in his words he was loyal and blunt, and whenever there were calamities or anomalies he always pointed to the facts and remonstrated face to face.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and outspoken; whenever omens appeared he spoke plainly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 而煬帝性多忌刻，齊王暕亦被猜嫌。

translations.literal: But Emperor Yang was by nature much given to suspicion and harshness, and Prince Xiu of Qi was also viewed with distrust.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was suspicious by nature, and Prince Xiu of Qi likewise fell under suspicion.

sentences.zh: 質子儉時為齊王屬，帝謂質曰：「汝不能一心事我，乃使兒事齊王，何向背如此邪？」

translations.literal: Zhi's son Jian was then an aide to Prince Qi, and the emperor said to Zhi, "You cannot serve me with a single heart—you make your son serve Prince Qi. Why this turning back and forth?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Jian served Prince Qi, and the emperor said to Zhi, "You cannot give me your whole loyalty—you set your son to serve Prince Qi. Why this divided allegiance?"

sentences.zh: 質曰：「臣事陛下，子事齊王，實是一心，不敢有二。」

translations.literal: Zhi said, "Your servant serves Your Majesty; my son serves Prince Qi—it is in truth one heart, and I dare not be of two minds."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied, "I serve Your Majesty; my son serves Prince Qi. It is one loyalty, not two."

sentences.zh: 帝怒不解，由是出為合水令。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger did not abate, and on that account Zhi was sent out as Magistrate of Heshui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not be appeased and sent Zhi out as Magistrate of Heshui.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝親伐遼東，征詣行在所。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor personally campaigned against Liaodong and summoned him to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor marched personally against Liaodong and summoned Zhi to the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 至臨渝謁見，帝謂質曰：「朕承先旨，親事高麗，度其土地人民，才當我一郡，卿以為克不？」

translations.literal: When he arrived at Linyu and was received in audience, the emperor said to Zhi, "I follow the prior intent and personally take Goguryeo in hand; judging its land and people, they amount to no more than one of our commanderies—do you think it can be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: At Linyu the emperor asked Zhi, "I follow my predecessor's intent in attacking Goguryeo myself. Its land and people are no more than one of our commanderies—do you think we can conquer it?"

sentences.zh: 質對曰：「以臣管窺，伐之可克，切有愚見，不願陛下親行。」

translations.literal: Zhi replied, "By my narrow view, the campaign can succeed, but I have a foolish opinion: I do not wish Your Majesty to go in person."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi answered, "By my limited judgment the war can be won, but I would rather Your Majesty not go yourself."

sentences.zh: 帝作色曰：「朕今總兵至此，豈可未見賊而自退也？」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said, "I have now gathered the army here—how can I withdraw before even seeing the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed and said, "I have brought the army this far—how can I turn back before even seeing the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 質又曰：「陛下若行，慮損軍威。

translations.literal: Zhi said again, "If Your Majesty goes, I fear the army's prestige will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi added, "If Your Majesty goes in person, I fear it will weaken the army's prestige.

sentences.zh: 臣猶願安駕住此，命驍將勇士指授規模，倍道兼行，出其不意。

translations.literal: Your servant would still wish Your Majesty to remain here in safety, appoint fierce generals and brave warriors to direct the plan, march by forced stages, and strike where they do not expect.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather Your Majesty stay here safely and send bold generals to direct the campaign, marching by forced stages to strike where the enemy does not expect.

sentences.zh: 事宜在速，緩必無功。」

translations.literal: The matter depends on speed; if delayed, there will certainly be no success."
translations.idiomatic: Speed is everything; delay will bring failure."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅曰：「汝既難行，可住此也。」

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased, said, "Since you find it hard to go, you may stay here."
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor said, "Since you find it hard to go, stay here."

sentences.zh: 及師還，授太史令。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Zhi was appointed Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Zhi was appointed Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 九年，複征高麗，又問質曰：「今段複何如？」

translations.literal: In the ninth year Goguryeo was attacked again, and the emperor again asked Zhi, "How does this expedition look now?"
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, with Goguryeo attacked again, the emperor asked Zhi, "How does this campaign look now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣實愚迷，猶執前見。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant is truly foolish and confused and still holds to my earlier view.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I am dull and still hold to my earlier view.

sentences.zh: 陛下若親動萬乘，糜費實多。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty personally moves the imperial chariot, the expense will indeed be great."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty leads the imperial host in person, the cost will be enormous."

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「我自行尚不能克，直遣人去，豈有成功也！」

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily, "If I go myself it still cannot be taken—would sending others alone ever succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "If I go myself and still cannot win, how could sending others alone succeed!"

sentences.zh: 帝遂行。

translations.literal: The emperor then went.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went anyway.

sentences.zh: 既而禮部尚書楊玄感據黎陽反，兵部侍郎斛斯政奔高麗，帝大懼，遽而西還，謂質曰：「卿前不許我行，當為此耳。

translations.literal: Before long Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan seized Liyang in rebellion, and Vice Minister of War Husi Zheng fled to Goguryeo; the emperor was greatly afraid, hurried back west, and said to Zhi, "You would not let me go—it was for this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan rebelled at Liyang and Vice Minister of War Husi Zheng fled to Goguryeo. The emperor hurried west in alarm and told Zhi, "You would not let me go—it was for this.

sentences.zh: 今者玄感其成事乎？」

translations.literal: Will Xuangan succeed now?"
translations.idiomatic: Will Xuangan succeed now?"

sentences.zh: 質曰：「玄感地勢雖隆，德望非素，因百姓之勞苦，冀僥倖而成功。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "Xuangan's position is lofty in terrain but not in moral standing; relying on the people's toil and hardship, he hopes for success by chance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "Xuangan holds strong ground but no moral authority; he relies on popular exhaustion and hopes for a lucky break.

sentences.zh: 今天下一家，未易可動。」

translations.literal: Now the realm is one family—it will not be easy to move."
translations.idiomatic: The realm is united; he will not easily prevail."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「熒惑入鬥如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What of Mars entering the Dipper?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What of Mars entering the Dipper?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「鬥，楚之分，玄感之所封也。

translations.literal: He replied, "The Dipper is the division of Chu—the territory Xuangan was enfeoffed in.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The Dipper marks the Chu region—Xuangan's fief.

sentences.zh: 今火色衰謝，終必無成。」

translations.literal: Now the fire star's color is fading; in the end he will certainly not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: The fire star is fading; he will not succeed in the end."

sentences.zh: 十年，帝自西京將往東都，質諫曰：「比歲伐遼，民實勞敝，陛下宜鎮撫關內，使百姓畢力歸農。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, as the emperor was about to go from the Western Capital to the Eastern Capital, Zhi remonstrated, "In recent years the Liaodong campaigns have truly exhausted the people; Your Majesty should pacify and settle the lands within the passes and let the common people devote their full strength to farming.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, as the emperor prepared to leave the Western Capital for the Eastern Capital, Zhi remonstrated, "Years of Liaodong campaigns have exhausted the people. Your Majesty should settle the heartland and let the people return fully to farming.

sentences.zh: 三五年間，令四海少得豐實，然後巡省，於事為宜。

translations.literal: Within three to five years, let the four seas attain some measure of abundance; then a tour of inspection would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In three to five years, when the realm has regained some prosperity, a tour would be appropriate.

sentences.zh: 陛下思之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, consider this."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, please consider this."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，質辭疾不從。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; Zhi pleaded illness and refused to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased; Zhi pleaded illness and refused to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，怒，遣使馳傳，鎖質詣行在所。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he was angry and sent a messenger by post relay to shackle Zhi and bring him to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor sent a courier to shackle Zhi and bring him to the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 至東都，詔令下獄，竟死獄中。

translations.literal: When he reached the Eastern Capital, an edict ordered him thrown into prison, and in the end he died there.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital an edict sent him to prison, where he died.

sentences.zh: 子儉，亦傳父業，兼有學識。

translations.literal: His son Jian also inherited his father's craft and possessed learning as well.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian inherited his father's arts and had scholarly attainments of his own.

sentences.zh: 仕曆襄武令、元德太子學士、齊王屬。

translations.literal: He served as Magistrate of Xiangwu, Academician to the Crown Prince of Yuande, and Aide to Prince Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Magistrate of Xiangwu, Academician to the Crown Prince of Yuande, and Aide to Prince Qi.

sentences.zh: 義甯初，為太史令，時有盧太翼、耿詢，並以星曆知名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yining he became Grand Astrologer; at that time Lu Taiyi and Geng Xun were both famed for astronomy and the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yining he became Grand Astrologer; Lu Taiyi and Geng Xun were then both renowned for astronomy and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 盧太翼，字協昭，河間人也，本姓章仇氏。

translations.literal: Lu Taiyi, courtesy name Xiezhao, was a man of Hejian; his original surname was Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Taiyi, styled Xiezhao, came from Hejian; his original surname was Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 七歲詣學，日誦數千言，州裡號曰神童。

translations.literal: At seven he went to school and recited several thousand characters a day; the district and village called him a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he entered school and recited several thousand characters daily; neighbors called him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 及長，閒居味道，不求榮利。

translations.literal: When grown, he lived in retirement savoring the Way and sought neither glory nor profit.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he lived in seclusion, savoring the Way, and sought neither fame nor gain.

sentences.zh: 博綜群書，爰及佛道，皆得其精微。

translations.literal: He mastered many books, extending even to Buddhism and Daoism, and attained their subtle essence in all.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered many books, including Buddhist and Daoist texts, reaching their subtle core in each.

sentences.zh: 尤善占候算曆之術。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in prognostication, observation, calculation, and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in prognostication, observation, calculation, and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 隱于白鹿山，數年徙居林慮山茱萸澗。

translations.literal: He hid on Mount Bailu; after several years he moved to Zhuyu Stream in the Linlu Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Mount Bailu, then after several years moved to Zhuyu Stream in the Linlu Mountains.

sentences.zh: 請業者自遠而至，初無所拒，後憚其煩，逃於五臺山。

translations.literal: Those who came from afar to study with him were at first never refused; later, fearing the bother, he fled to Mount Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: Students came from afar; at first he never refused them, but later, weary of the crowd, he fled to Mount Wutai.

sentences.zh: 地多藥物，與弟子數人廬於岩下，蕭然絕世，以為神仙可致。

translations.literal: The place abounded in medicinal herbs; with several disciples he built a hut beneath the cliffs, utterly removed from the world, believing that immortals could be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Medicinal herbs grew there in abundance; he built a hut on the cliffs with several disciples, cut off from the world, believing immortality attainable.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇聞而召之，太翼知太子必不為嗣，謂所親曰：「吾拘逼而來，不知所稅駕也！」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong heard of him and summoned him; Taiyi knew the prince would certainly not succeed as heir and said to those close to him, "I have been forced here—I do not know where I shall alight!"
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong summoned him; Taiyi knew the prince would never succeed and told his intimates, "I have been dragged here—I do not know where this will end!"

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，坐法當死，高祖惜其才而不害，配為官奴。

translations.literal: When the prince was deposed, Taiyi was liable to capital punishment; Gaozu valued his talent and did not harm him, assigning him instead as a government slave.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was deposed, Taiyi faced death; Gaozu spared his talent and made him a government slave instead.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃釋。

translations.literal: After a long while he was released.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was freed.

sentences.zh: 其後目盲，以手摸書而知其字。

translations.literal: Later he went blind and could know characters by feeling books with his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went blind and could read by feeling the characters with his hand.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，高祖將避暑仁壽宮，太翼固諫不納，至於再三。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou, when Gaozu was about to take the summer retreat at Renshou Palace, Taiyi firmly remonstrated and was not heeded, even after repeating his advice again and again.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Renshou, as Gaozu prepared to summer at Renshou Palace, Taiyi remonstrated firmly and was ignored, even after repeating himself again and again.

sentences.zh: 太翼曰：「臣愚豈敢飾詞，但恐是行鑾輿不反。」

translations.literal: Taiyi said, "Your servant is foolish—how dare I dress up my words? I only fear that on this journey the imperial carriage will not return."
translations.idiomatic: Taiyi said, "I am no flatterer—I only fear the imperial carriage will not return from this journey."

sentences.zh: 高祖大怒，系之長安獄，期還而斬之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly enraged, bound him in the prison at Chang'an, and set a date for his return and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was furious, imprisoned him in Chang'an, and set a date to behead him on his return.

sentences.zh: 高祖至宮寢疾，臨崩，謂皇太子曰：「章仇翼，非常人也，前後言事，未嘗不中。

translations.literal: Gaozu fell ill at the palace; on his deathbed he said to the crown prince, "Zhangqiu Yi is no ordinary man—what he has said before and after has never missed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu fell ill at the palace; on his deathbed he told the crown prince, "Zhangqiu Yi is no ordinary man—his predictions have never missed.

sentences.zh: 吾來日道當不反，今果至此，爾宜釋之。」

translations.literal: I said I would not return on this journey, and now it has indeed come to this; you should release him."
translations.idiomatic: I said I would not return, and so it has proved; you should release him."

sentences.zh: 及煬帝即位，漢王諒反，帝以問之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Prince Xiu of Han rebelled, and the emperor questioned Taiyi about it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne and Prince Xiu of Han rebelled, the emperor asked Taiyi about it.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「上稽玄象，下參人事，何所能為？」

translations.literal: He replied, "Looking up to the dark signs above and down to human affairs below—what can he accomplish?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Judging heaven above and men below—what can he accomplish?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，諒果敗。

translations.literal: Before long Prince Xiu was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Prince Xiu was indeed defeated.

sentences.zh: 帝常從容言及天下氏族，謂太翼曰：「卿姓章仇，四嶽之胄，與盧同源。」

translations.literal: The emperor often spoke at leisure of the clans of the realm and said to Taiyi, "Your surname is Zhangqiu—you are descended from the Four Peaks and share the same origin as the Lu clan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often spoke of great clans and told Taiyi, "Your surname Zhangqiu marks you as descended from the Four Peaks, of the same origin as the Lu."

sentences.zh: 於是賜姓為盧氏。

translations.literal: He then granted him the surname Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him the surname Lu.

sentences.zh: 大業九年，從駕至遼東，太翼言於帝曰：「黎陽有兵氣。」

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye, accompanying the imperial progress to Liaodong, Taiyi said to the emperor, "There is a martial aura at Liyang."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daye, on the Liaodong campaign, Taiyi told the emperor, "There is a martial aura at Liyang."

sentences.zh: 後數日而玄感反書聞，帝甚異之，數加賞賜。

translations.literal: Several days later word came of Xuangan's rebellion; the emperor was greatly astonished and repeatedly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Days later came word of Xuangan's rebellion; the emperor was astonished and richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 太翼所言天文之事，不可稱數，關諸秘密，世莫得聞。

translations.literal: What Taiyi said of celestial matters cannot be counted; it touched on secrets, and the world could not hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyi's predictions about heaven were countless and touched state secrets the world never heard.

sentences.zh: 後數載，卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: Several years later he died at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 耿詢，字敦信，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: Geng Xun, courtesy name Dunxin, was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Xun, styled Dunxin, came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 滑稽辯給，伎巧絕人。

translations.literal: He was witty, fluent, and clever beyond ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: He was witty, eloquent, and surpassingly ingenious.

sentences.zh: 陳後主之世，以客從東衡州刺史王勇於嶺南。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Houzhu of Chen he followed as a guest-guest Governor Wang Yong of East Heng Province into Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen Emperor Houzhu he followed Governor Wang Yong of East Heng Province to Lingnan as a client.

sentences.zh: 勇卒，詢不歸，遂與諸越相結，皆得其歡心。

translations.literal: When Yong died, Xun did not return home but instead joined with the various Yue peoples and won the favor of them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong died, Xun did not return north but bonded with the Yue peoples and won their affection.

sentences.zh: 會郡俚反叛，推詢為主。

translations.literal: When the commandery's tribal leaders rebelled, they made Xun their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal leaders in the commandery rebelled, they made Xun their chief.

sentences.zh: 柱國王世積討擒之，罪當誅。

translations.literal: Pillar of State Wang Shiji captured him in a punitive campaign; the crime merited execution.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of State Wang Shiji captured him in punitive action; the crime called for death.

sentences.zh: 自言有巧思，世積釋之，以為家奴。

translations.literal: He declared that he possessed ingenious skill; Shiji released him and made him a household slave.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed ingenious skill; Shiji spared him and kept him as a household slave.

sentences.zh: 久之，見其故人高智寶以玄象直太史，詢從之受天文算術。

translations.literal: After a long while he saw his old acquaintance Gao Zhibao serving as Direct Astrologer on celestial signs and studied astronomy and calculation under him.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he found his old acquaintance Gao Zhibao serving as Direct Astrologer and studied astronomy and calculation under him.

sentences.zh: 詢創意造渾天儀，不假人力，以水轉之，施於暗室中，使智寶外候天時，合如符契。

translations.literal: Xun devised and built an armillary sphere that needed no human power but was turned by water; set up in a dark room, when Zhibao observed the heavens outside, the two matched as if by tally.
translations.idiomatic: Xun invented a water-driven armillary sphere needing no human hand; placed in a dark room, when Zhibao watched the sky outside, the two matched perfectly.

sentences.zh: 世積知而奏之，高祖配詢為官奴，給使太史局。

translations.literal: Shiji learned of it and memorialized; Gaozu assigned Xun as a government slave and put him to service in the Astrologer's Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji reported it; Gaozu made Xun a government slave and assigned him to the Astrologer's Bureau.

sentences.zh: 後賜蜀王秀，從往益州，秀甚信之。

translations.literal: Later he was granted to Prince Xiu of Shu and followed him to Yizhou; the prince trusted him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was given to Prince Xiu of Shu and followed him to Yizhou, where the prince trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及秀廢，複當誅，何稠言于高祖曰：「耿詢之巧，思若有神，臣誠為朝廷惜之。」

translations.literal: When the prince was deposed, Xun again faced execution; He Chou said to Gaozu, "Geng Xun's ingenuity is almost divine—I truly regret this for the court."
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was deposed, Xun again faced death; He Chou told Gaozu, "Geng Xun's ingenuity is near miraculous—the court would be the poorer for losing him."

sentences.zh: 上於是特原其罪。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon specially pardoned his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 詢作馬上刻漏，世稱其妙。

translations.literal: Xun made a clepsydra for use on horseback, and the age praised its marvel.
translations.idiomatic: Xun built a portable clepsydra for use on horseback, and contemporaries marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，進欹器，帝善之，放為良民。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Xun presented a tilt-vessel; the emperor approved and freed him as a common citizen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Xun presented a tilt-vessel; the emperor approved and freed him as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，授右尚方署監事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Supervisor of the Right Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was appointed Supervisor of the Right Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 七年，車駕東征，詢上書曰：「遼東不可討，師必無功。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, as the imperial carriage campaigned east, Xun memorialized, "Liaodong cannot be attacked; the army will certainly fail."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, on the eastern campaign, Xun memorialized, "Liaodong cannot be subdued; the army will fail."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命左右斬之，何稠苦諫得免。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered his attendants to behead him; He Chou's bitter remonstrance saved him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered him beheaded; He Chou's desperate remonstrance saved him.

sentences.zh: 及平壤之敗，帝以詢言為中，以詢守太史丞。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Pyongyang the emperor considered Xun's words correct and made him Acting Director of the Astrologer's Office.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Pyongyang the emperor judged Xun right and made him Acting Director of the Astrologer's Office.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之後，從至黎陽，謂其妻曰：「近觀人事，遠察天文，宇文必敗，李氏當王，吾知所歸矣。」

translations.literal: After Yuwen Huaji's regicide, following him to Liyang, he said to his wife, "Observing men close at hand and the heavens far off, Yuwen will fail and the Li will reign—I know where to go now."
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji's regicide, at Liyang he told his wife, "Watching men near and heaven far, Yuwen will fail and the Li will rise—I know where to go."

sentences.zh: 詢欲去之，為化及所殺。

translations.literal: Xun wished to leave but was killed by Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Xun tried to leave but Huaji killed him.

sentences.zh: 著《鳥情占》一卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He authored Bird-Omen Prognostics in one scroll, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Bird-Omen Prognostics in one scroll, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 韋鼎，字超盛，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Wei Ding Wei Ding, courtesy name Chaosheng, was a man of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ding, styled Chaosheng, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 高祖玄，隱于商山，因而歸宋。

translations.literal: His ancestor Xuan hid on Mount Shang and thereafter entered the service of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Xuan withdrew to Mount Shang and later entered Song service.

sentences.zh: 祖睿，梁開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rui was Senior Grand Master of State with the Opening of an Office under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rui served Liang as Senior Grand Master of State with the Opening of an Office.

sentences.zh: 父正，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Zheng was Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng was Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鼎少通脫，博涉經史，明陰陽逆刺，尤善相術。

translations.literal: Ding from youth was open and unbound, broadly versed in the classics and histories, understood yin-yang and the cycles of reversal, and was especially skilled in physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ding was free-spirited and widely read in the classics and histories; he understood yin-yang and reversal cycles and was especially skilled in physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，起家湘東王法曹參軍。

translations.literal: He served Liang, beginning his career as Legal Officer Aide to Prince Yi of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he began as Legal Officer Aide to Prince Yi of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，水漿不入口者五日，哀毀過禮，殆將滅性。

translations.literal: When his father died he took no food or drink for five days; his grief exceeded the rites and nearly destroyed his life.
translations.idiomatic: At his father's death he took no food or drink for five days; his grief exceeded the rites and nearly cost him his life.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為邵陵王主簿。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Secretary to Prince Shao of Ling.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he served as Secretary to Prince Shao of Ling.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，鼎兄昂卒于京城，鼎負屍出，寄于中興寺。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Ding's elder brother Ang died in the capital; Ding carried the corpse out and placed it at Zhongxing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Ding's elder brother Ang died in the capital; Ding carried the body out and laid it at Zhongxing Temple.

sentences.zh: 求棺無所得，鼎哀憤慟哭，忽見江中有物，流至鼎所，鼎切異之。

translations.literal: He could find no coffin; in grief and rage Ding wept bitterly, when suddenly he saw something in the river drifting toward him, and he was deeply astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to find a coffin, Ding wept in grief and rage until something in the river drifted toward him—he was astonished.

sentences.zh: 往見，乃新棺也，因以充殮。

translations.literal: Going to look, it was a new coffin, and he used it for the encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: He found it was a new coffin and used it for the burial.

sentences.zh: 元帝聞之，以為精誠所感。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan heard of it, he considered it a response to sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan took it as a response to sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，司徒王僧辯以為戶曹屬，曆太尉掾、大司馬從事、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, Minister of Works Wang Sengbian made him a member of the Households Bureau; he served successively as Aide to the Grand Commandant, Staff member to the Grand Marshal, and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was pacified, Wang Sengbian made him a member of the Households Bureau; he rose through posts as Aide to the Grand Commandant, staff to the Grand Marshal, and Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝在南徐州，鼎望氣知其當王，遂寄孥焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Chen was at South Xuzhou; Ding read the qi and knew he would become king, and so sent his wife and children to join him there.
translations.idiomatic: At South Xuzhou Ding read the qi and knew Chen Wudi would become king, and sent his family to join him.

sentences.zh: 因謂陳武帝曰：「明年有大臣誅死，後四歲，梁其代終，天之歷數當歸舜後。

translations.literal: He therefore said to Emperor Wu of Chen, "Next year a great minister will be executed; four years later Liang's mandate will end, and Heaven's succession should return to the line of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: He told Chen Wudi, "Next year a great minister will die by execution; four years later Liang's mandate ends and Heaven's succession returns to Shun's line.

sentences.zh: 昔周滅殷氏，封媯滿于宛丘，其裔子孫因為陳氏。

translations.literal: Formerly when Zhou destroyed the Yin, it enfeoffed Gui Man at Wancheng; his descendants became the Chen clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou destroyed Yin it enfeoffed Gui Man at Wancheng; his descendants became the Chen clan.

sentences.zh: 僕觀明公天縱神武，繼絕統者，無乃是乎！」

translations.literal: Your servant sees that my lord is Heaven-endowed and divinely martial—the one to restore a broken succession—could it not be you!"
translations.idiomatic: I see in you Heaven's gift and divine martial prowess—the restorer of a broken line. Could it not be you?"

sentences.zh: 武帝陰有圖僧辯意，聞其言，大喜，因而定策。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu secretly already intended to move against Sengbian; hearing these words he was greatly pleased and on that account fixed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi already secretly planned against Sengbian; hearing this he was delighted and fixed his strategy.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜黃門侍郎，俄遷司農卿、司徒右長史、貞威將軍，領安右晉安王長史、行府國事，轉廷尉卿。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; soon he was promoted to Minister of Agriculture, Senior Secretary on the Right of the Minister of Education, General of Manifest Prestige, concurrently Chief Secretary to Prince Jin'an of Anyou and acting administrator of the princely fief, then transferred to Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the abdication he became Vice Director of the Secretariat, then Minister of Agriculture, Senior Secretary on the Right, General of Manifest Prestige, Chief Secretary to Prince Jin'an, acting fief administrator, then Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 太建中，為聘周主使，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he served as envoy to betroth a Zhou princess and was given the added title Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he was envoy to betroth a Zhou princess and received the added title Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋為秘書監、宣遠將軍，轉臨海王長史，行吳興郡事。

translations.literal: Soon he became Director of the Secretariat, General of Extended Reach, transferred to Chief Secretary to Prince Linhai, and acting administrator of Wuxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Director of the Secretariat, General of Extended Reach, Chief Secretary to Prince Linhai, and acting administrator of Wuxing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 入為太府卿。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 至德初，鼎盡質貨田宅，寓居僧寺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, Ding pawned all his goods, fields, and houses and lodged in a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhide he pawned all his property and lodged in a temple.

sentences.zh: 友人大匠卿毛彪問其故，答曰：「江東王氣盡於此矣。

translations.literal: His friend Grand Master of Works Mao Biao asked the reason, and he answered, "The kingly qi of Jiangdong is exhausted here.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Mao Biao, Grand Master of Works, asked why; he answered, "Jiangdong's kingly qi is exhausted here.

sentences.zh: 吾與爾當葬長安。

translations.literal: You and I shall be buried in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: You and I shall be buried in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 期運將及，故破產耳。」

translations.literal: The turn of fate is near—that is why I have ruined my estate."
translations.idiomatic: The turn of fate is near—that is why I have ruined my estate."

sentences.zh: 初，鼎之聘周也，嘗與高祖相遇，鼎謂高祖曰：「觀公容貌，故非常人，而神監深遠，亦非群賢所逮也。

translations.literal: When Ding first went on the mission to Zhou, he once met Gaozu and said to him, "Judging your countenance, you are no ordinary man; your spiritual insight is deep and far-reaching and not matched by the crowd of worthies either.
translations.idiomatic: On his Zhou mission Ding once met Gaozu and said, "Your face is no ordinary man's; your insight is deep beyond other worthies.

sentences.zh: 不久必大貴，貴則天下一家，歲一周天，老夫當委質。

translations.literal: Before long you will rise to great honor; when honored, the realm will be one family. When a year completes its cycle through Heaven, this old man will offer his allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon you will rise to great honor; when honored the realm will be one family. When a year completes its heavenly cycle, this old man will offer allegiance.

sentences.zh: 公相不可言，願深自愛。」

translations.literal: Your physiognomy cannot be spoken of—please cherish yourself deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Your fate cannot be spoken of—please cherish yourself deeply."

sentences.zh: 及陳平，上馳召之，授上儀同三司，待遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, the emperor urgently summoned him and appointed him Senior Grand Master of State with the Three Excellencies' Honors, treating him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell the emperor summoned him and appointed him Senior Grand Master of State with the Three Excellencies' Honors, treating him generously.

sentences.zh: 上每與公王宴賞，鼎恆預焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor feasted and rewarded the princes and dukes, Ding was always present.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor feasted princes and dukes, Ding was always present.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗從容謂之曰：「韋世康與公相去遠近？」

translations.literal: Gaozu once said to him at leisure, "How close or distant is Wei Shikang to you?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once asked him at leisure, "How close are you to Wei Shikang?"

sentences.zh: 鼎對曰：「臣宗族分派，南北孤絕，自生以來，未嘗訪問。」

translations.literal: Ding replied, "Your servant's clan split into branches; north and south are cut off from each other. From birth I have never made inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: Ding replied, "Our clan split; north and south are cut off. From birth I have never inquired."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公百世卿族，何得爾也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your clan is a hundred-generation ministerial house—how can it be so?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your clan is a hundred-generation ministerial house—how can this be?"

sentences.zh: 乃命官給酒肴，遣世康與鼎還杜陵，樂飲十餘日。

translations.literal: He then ordered officials to supply wine and food and sent Shikang back to Duling with Ding to feast together for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered wine and food supplied and sent Shikang with Ding to Duling to feast for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 鼎乃考校昭穆，自楚太傅孟以下二十餘世，作《韋氏譜》七卷。

translations.literal: Ding then verified the generations from Chu Grand Tutor Meng downward for more than twenty generations and compiled the Genealogy of the Wei Clan in seven scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Ding verified the generations from Chu Grand Tutor Meng downward for twenty-plus generations and compiled the Genealogy of the Wei Clan in seven scrolls.

sentences.zh: 時蘭陵公主寡，上為之求夫，選親衛柳述及蕭瑒等以示於鼎。

translations.literal: At that time Princess of Lanling was widowed; the emperor sought a husband for her and selected Imperial Guard Liu Shu and Xiao Yang among others to show to Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Lanling was widowed; the emperor selected Imperial Guard Liu Shu and Xiao Yang among others to show Ding.

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「瑒當封侯，而無貴妻之相，述亦通顯，而守位不終。」

translations.literal: Ding said, "Yang will be enfeoffed as a marquis but has not the physiognomy of a noble wife; Shu also will rise to prominence but will not hold rank to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "Yang will be enfeoffed but lacks a noble wife's physiognomy; Shu will rise but not hold rank to the end."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「位由我耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Rank is in my hands."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Rank is in my hands."

sentences.zh: 遂以主降述。

translations.literal: He then gave the princess in marriage to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave the princess to Shu in marriage.

sentences.zh: 上又問鼎：「諸兒誰得嗣？」

translations.literal: The emperor again asked Ding, "Which of my sons will succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked, "Which son will succeed?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「至尊、皇后所最愛者，即當與之，非臣敢預知也。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Whomever Your Majesty and the empress love most—that one will receive it; your servant dare not presume to know beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Whomever Your Majesty and the empress love most—that one will receive it; I dare not presume to know."

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「不肯顯言乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "You won't speak plainly, then?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed, "You won't speak plainly?"

sentences.zh: 開皇十二年，除光州刺史，以仁義教導，務弘清靜。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaihuang he was appointed Governor of Guang Prefecture and taught by benevolence and righteousness, striving to promote clarity and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year twelve he became Governor of Guang Prefecture, teaching benevolence and righteousness and promoting clarity and quiet.

sentences.zh: 州中有土豪，外修邊幅，而內行不軌，常為劫盜。

translations.literal: In the prefecture was a local strongman who outwardly cultivated proper appearance but inwardly acted without principle and often robbed and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: A local strongman in the prefecture kept proper appearances outwardly but robbed and plundered inwardly.

sentences.zh: 鼎于都會時謂之曰：「卿是好人，那忽作賊？」

translations.literal: At a public gathering Ding said to him, "You are a good man—why suddenly turn bandit?"
translations.idiomatic: At a public gathering Ding said to him, "You are a good man—why turn bandit?"

sentences.zh: 因條其徒黨謀議逗留，其人驚懼，即自首伏。

translations.literal: He then listed his gang's plots and delays; the man was alarmed and immediately confessed.
translations.idiomatic: He listed the gang's plots; the man was alarmed and confessed.

sentences.zh: 又有人客遊，通主家之妾，及其還去，妾盜珍物，於夜亡，尋于草中為人所殺。

translations.literal: Another case: a traveling guest had an affair with his host's concubine; when he left, the concubine stole valuables and fled by night, and was later found killed in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: A traveling guest had an affair with his host's concubine; when he left she stole valuables and fled by night, and was later found killed in the grass.

sentences.zh: 主家知客與妾通，因告客殺之。

translations.literal: The host knew the guest had been intimate with the concubine and therefore accused the guest of the murder.
translations.idiomatic: The host knew of the affair and accused the guest of murder.

sentences.zh: 縣司鞫問，具得奸狀，因斷客死。

translations.literal: The county office interrogated and fully established the adultery, then sentenced the guest to death.
translations.idiomatic: The county established the adultery and sentenced the guest to death.

sentences.zh: 獄成，上於鼎，鼎覽之曰：「此客實奸，而殺非也。

translations.literal: When the case was complete it was submitted to Ding; Ding read it and said, "This guest was indeed adulterous, but he did not commit the killing.
translations.idiomatic: Ding read the completed case and said, "The guest was adulterous but did not kill.

sentences.zh: 乃某寺僧詃妾盜物，令奴殺之，贓在某處。」

translations.literal: It was a monk at a certain temple who seduced the concubine to steal, had a slave kill her, and the loot is at a certain place."
translations.idiomatic: A monk at a certain temple seduced the concubine to steal, had a slave kill her, and the loot is at a certain place."

sentences.zh: 即放此客，遣掩僧，並獲贓物。

translations.literal: He immediately released the guest, sent men to seize the monk, and recovered the stolen goods.
translations.idiomatic: He released the guest, seized the monk, and recovered the stolen goods.

sentences.zh: 自是部內肅然不言，鹹稱其有神，道無拾遺。

translations.literal: From then on within the commandery all was quiet and none spoke of it; all praised him as having divine power, and nothing lost on the road was picked up.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the commandery was quiet; all praised his divine insight, and nothing lost on the road was picked up.

sentences.zh: 尋追入京，以年老多病，累加優賜。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to the capital; being old and often ill, he received repeated special favors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled; old and often ill, he received repeated special favors.

sentences.zh: 頃之，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 來和，字弘順，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Lai He, courtesy name Hongshun, was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lai He, styled Hongshun, came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少好相術，所言多驗。

translations.literal: From youth he loved physiognomy; what he said often came true.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved physiognomy; his words often came true.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護引之左右，由是出入公卿之門。

translations.literal: Grand Minister Yuwen Hu kept him at his side, and thereby he passed in and out of the gates of dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister Yuwen Hu kept him at his side, and he passed through the gates of dukes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 初為夏官府下士，累遷少卜上士，購爵安定鄉男。

translations.literal: At first he served as xiashi, Lower Serviceman, in the Xiaguan Office. He was repeatedly promoted to shaobu shangshi, Senior Serviceman for Minor Divination, and purchased the noble title Baron of Anding Township.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as xiashi, Lower Serviceman, in the Xiaguan Office. He was repeatedly promoted to shaobu shangshi, Senior Serviceman for Minor Divination, and purchased the noble title Baron of Anding Township.

sentences.zh: 遷畿伯下大夫，進封洹水縣男。
