translations.literal: He was transferred to Lower Grand Master of the Ji Domain, and advanced to Baron of Huanshui County.
translations.idiomatic: He became Lower Grand Master of the Ji Domain and advanced to Baron of Huanshui County.

sentences.zh: 高祖微時，來詣和相，和待人去，謂高祖曰：「公當王有四海。」

translations.literal: When Gaozu was still obscure, Lai came to have He read his physiognomy; after the guest left, He said to Gaozu, "My lord will become king and possess all within the seas."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was still obscure, Lai had He read his face; after Lai left, He told Gaozu, "You will become king and possess all within the seas."

sentences.zh: 及為丞相，拜儀同，既受禪，進爵為子。

translations.literal: When he became Chancellor, He was appointed Senior Grand Master of State with the Three Excellencies' Honors; after receiving the abdication his rank was advanced to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became Chancellor, He was appointed Senior Grand Master of State; after the abdication his rank advanced to Viscount.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，和上表自陳曰：

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, He submitted a memorial in his own person:
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaihuang, He submitted a personal memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣早奉龍顏，自周代天和三年已來，數蒙陛下顧問，當時具言至尊膺圖受命，光宅區宇。

translations.literal: Your servant early received the dragon countenance; since the third year of Tianhe in Zhou I have repeatedly received Your Majesty's inquiries, and at that time fully stated that Your Majesty would receive the mandate, illuminate the realm, and dwell in the domain.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant early received the dragon countenance; since Zhou Tianhe year three I have repeatedly been consulted, and then fully stated that Your Majesty would receive the mandate and illuminate the realm.

sentences.zh: 此乃天授，非由人事所及。

translations.literal: This is Heaven's grant and not within the reach of human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This is Heaven's grant, not within human reach.

sentences.zh: 臣無勞效，坐致五品，二十餘年。

translations.literal: Your servant had no meritorious service yet sat at the fifth rank for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant had no merit yet sat at the fifth rank for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 臣是何人，敢不慚懼！

translations.literal: What kind of man is your servant that he dare not feel shame and fear!
translations.idiomatic: What kind of man am I that I dare not feel shame and fear!

sentences.zh: 愚臣不任區區之至，謹錄陛下龍潛之時，臣有所言一得，書之秘府，死無所恨。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant cannot bear this utmost sincerity; I respectfully record what Your Majesty said when still in obscurity that your servant got right once, and place it in the secret archive—then I can die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear this utmost sincerity; I respectfully record what Your Majesty said in obscurity that I got right once, and place it in the secret archive—then I can die without regret.

sentences.zh: 昔陛下在周，嘗與永富公竇榮定語臣曰：「我聞有行聲，即識其人。」

translations.literal: Formerly when Your Majesty was in Zhou, he once spoke with Duke of Yongfu Dou Rongding and said to your servant, "I hear a man's gait and know the man."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in Zhou Your Majesty spoke with Duke of Yongfu Dou Rongding and told me, "I hear a man's gait and know the man."

sentences.zh: 臣當時即言公眼如曙星，無所不照，當王有天下，願忍誅殺。

translations.literal: Your servant then immediately said your eyes are like dawn stars, illuminating all—when you become king and possess the realm, please restrain executions.
translations.idiomatic: I then said your eyes are like dawn stars, illuminating all—when you become king, please restrain executions.

sentences.zh: 建德四年五月，周武帝在雲陽宮，謂臣曰：「諸公皆汝所識，隋公相祿何如？」

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Jiande, Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang Palace and said to your servant, "The lords are all men you know—how is Chancellor Sui's salary and emolument?"
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year four, fifth month, Zhou Wudi at Yunyang Palace asked me, "The lords are all men you know—how is Chancellor Sui's emolument?"

sentences.zh: 臣報武帝曰：「隋公止是守節人，可鎮一方。

translations.literal: Your servant reported to Emperor Wu, "Chancellor Sui is only a man who keeps his integrity—he can guard one region.
translations.idiomatic: I reported, "Chancellor Sui only keeps his integrity—he can guard one region.

sentences.zh: 若為將領，陳無不破。」

translations.literal: As a general leading troops, he would break Chen without fail."
translations.idiomatic: As a general he would break Chen without fail."

sentences.zh: 臣即于宮東南奏聞。

translations.literal: Your servant then reported this at the southeast of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: I then reported this at the palace's southeast.

sentences.zh: 陛下謂臣，此語不忘。

translations.literal: Your Majesty told your servant he never forgot these words.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty told me you never forgot these words.

sentences.zh: 明年，烏丸軌言于武帝曰：「隋公非人臣。」

translations.literal: The next year Wuji said to Emperor Wu, "Chancellor Sui is no subject of a king."
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wuji told Zhou Wudi, "Chancellor Sui is no subject of a king."

sentences.zh: 帝尋以問臣，臣知帝有疑，臣詭報曰：「是節臣，更無異相。」

translations.literal: The emperor soon asked your servant again; knowing the emperor had doubts, your servant falsely reported, "He is a man of integrity—there is no other physiognomy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon asked again; knowing he had doubts, I falsely reported, "He is a man of integrity—no other physiognomy."

sentences.zh: 于時王誼、梁彥光等知臣此語。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Yi, Liang Yanguang, and others knew your servant's words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, Liang Yanguang, and others knew my words then.

sentences.zh: 大象二年五月，至尊從永巷東門入，臣在永巷門東，北面立，陛下問臣曰：「我無災障不？」

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Daxiang, Your Majesty entered from the east gate of the Everlasting Lane; your servant stood north of the east gate of the Everlasting Lane, and Your Majesty asked, "Do I have no calamity or obstruction?"
translations.idiomatic: In Daxiang year two, fifth month, Your Majesty entered from the Everlasting Lane's east gate; I stood north of that gate, and Your Majesty asked, "Do I have no calamity?"

sentences.zh: 臣奏陛下曰：「公骨法氣色相應，天命已有付屬。」

translations.literal: Your servant memorialized, "Your bone structure and qi-color correspond—Heaven's mandate has already been entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: I memorialized, "Your bone structure and qi-color correspond—Heaven's mandate is already entrusted."

sentences.zh: 未幾，遂總百揆。

translations.literal: Before long you indeed took charge of all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long you indeed took charge of all affairs.

sentences.zh: 上覽之大悅，進位開府，購物五百段，米三百石，地十頃。

translations.literal: The emperor read it with great pleasure, promoted him to Grand Master with the Opening of an Office, and granted five hundred bolts of goods, three hundred shi of rice, and ten qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it with great pleasure, promoted him to Grand Master with the Opening of an Office, and granted five hundred bolts of goods, three hundred shi of rice, and ten qing of land.

sentences.zh: 和同郡韓則，嘗詣和相，和謂之曰：「後四五當得大官。」

translations.literal: Han Ze of the same commandery once came to He for a reading; He said to him, "In four or five years you will obtain a great office."
translations.idiomatic: Han Ze of the same commandery once came for a reading; He said, "In four or five years you will obtain a great office."

sentences.zh: 人初不知所謂。

translations.literal: People at first did not know what he meant.
translations.idiomatic: People at first did not know what he meant.

sentences.zh: 則至開皇十五年五月而終，人問其故，和曰：「十五年為三五，加以五月為四五。

translations.literal: Ze died in the fifth month of the fifteenth year of Kaihuang; when people asked the reason, He said, "Fifteen years is three-five; adding the fifth month makes four-five.
translations.idiomatic: Ze died in Kaihuang year fifteen, fifth month; when asked, He said, "Fifteen years is three-five; adding the fifth month makes four-five.

sentences.zh: 大官，槨也。」

translations.literal: Great office means coffin."
translations.idiomatic: Great office means coffin."

sentences.zh: 和言多此類。

translations.literal: He's words were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He's words were mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 著《相經》四十卷。

translations.literal: He authored Physiognomy Classic in forty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Physiognomy Classic in forty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 道士張賓、焦子順、雁門人董子華，此三人，當高祖龍潛時，並私謂高祖曰：「公當為天子，善自愛。」

translations.literal: The Daoist Zhang Bin, Jiao Zishun, and Dong Zihua of Yanmen—these three, when Gaozu was still in obscurity, all privately told Gaozu, "My lord will become Son of Heaven—please cherish yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Daoists Zhang Bin, Jiao Zishun, and Dong Zihua of Yanmen—all three, when Gaozu was in obscurity, privately told him, "You will become Son of Heaven—cherish yourself."

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，以賓為華州刺史，子順為開府，子華為上儀同。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he made Bin Inspector of Hua Prefecture, Zishun Kaifu, and Zihua Shangyitong.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne, he made Bin Inspector of Hua Prefecture, Zishun Kaifu, and Zihua Shangyitong.

sentences.zh: 蕭吉楊伯醜臨孝恭劉祐

translations.literal: Xiao Ji, Yang Bochou, Lin Xiaogong, Liu You
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji, Yang Bochou, Lin Xiaogong, and Liu You

sentences.zh: 蕭吉，字文休，梁武帝兄長沙宣武王懿之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji, courtesy name Wenxiu, was a grandson of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, elder brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji, styled Wenxiu, was a grandson of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, elder brother of Liang Wudi.

sentences.zh: 博學多通，尤精陰陽算術。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and mastered many fields, especially yin-yang and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and mastered many fields, especially yin-yang and calculation.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，遂歸於周，為儀同。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell he entered Zhou's service as Senior Grand Master of State with the Three Excellencies' Honors.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he entered Zhou service as Senior Grand Master of State.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，吉以朝政日亂，上書切諫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan, as court affairs grew daily corrupt, he submitted a memorial with stern remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan, as court affairs grew corrupt daily, he submitted stern remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 及隋受禪，進上儀同，以本官太常考定古今陰陽書。

translations.literal: When Sui received the abdication he was promoted to Senior Grand Master of State and, in his original office as Director of Ceremonies, was ordered to examine and fix ancient and modern books on yin-yang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui received the abdication he was promoted to Senior Grand Master of State and, as Director of Ceremonies, ordered to examine ancient and modern yin-yang books.

sentences.zh: 吉性孤峭，不與公卿相沉浮，又與楊素不協，由是擯落於世，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Ji was solitary and lofty, not mingling with dukes and ministers; he also did not get along with Yang Su, and on that account was cast aside in the world, depressed and unable to achieve his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was solitary and aloof, not mingling with ministers; he also clashed with Yang Su and was cast aside, depressed and unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 見上好徵祥之說，欲幹沒自進，遂矯其跡為悅媚焉。

translations.literal: Seeing that the emperor loved talk of auspicious signs, he wished to advance by currying favor and therefore disguised his manner into flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor loved auspicious signs, he wished to advance by flattery and disguised his manner accordingly.

sentences.zh: 開皇十四年上書曰：「今年歲在甲寅，十一月朔旦，以辛酉為冬至。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaihuang he submitted a memorial saying, "This year is jia-yin; on the first day of the eleventh month, xin-you is the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year fourteen he memorialized, "This year is jia-yin; on the first day of the eleventh month, xin-you is the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 來年乙卯，正月朔旦，以庚申為元日，冬至之日，即在朔旦。

translations.literal: Next year yi-mao: on the first day of the first month, geng-shen is New Year's Day; the day of the winter solstice falls on the first day of the month.
translations.idiomatic: Next year yi-mao: on the first day of the first month, geng-shen is New Year's Day; the winter solstice falls on the first day of the month.

sentences.zh: 《樂汁圖徵》雲：『天元十一月朔旦冬至，聖王受享祚。』

translations.literal: The Classic of Music's Portent of Juice says, 'On the first day of the eleventh month at the winter solstice, the sage king receives the mandate and enjoys the throne.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Music's Portent of Juice says, 'On the first day of the eleventh month at the winter solstice, the sage king receives the mandate and enjoys the throne.'

sentences.zh: 今聖主在位，居天元之首，而朔旦冬至，此慶一也。

translations.literal: Now the sage lord sits at Heaven's origin, and at the first day of the month comes the winter solstice—this is the first felicity.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sage lord sits at Heaven's origin, and at the first day of the month comes the winter solstice—this is the first felicity.

sentences.zh: 辛酉之日，即是至尊本命，辛德在丙，此十一月建丙子。

translations.literal: The day xin-you is precisely Your Majesty's natal day; xin's virtue is in bing—this eleventh month establishes bing-zi.
translations.idiomatic: The day xin-you is Your Majesty's natal day; xin's virtue is in bing—this eleventh month establishes bing-zi.

sentences.zh: 酉德在寅，正月建寅為本命，與月德合，而居元朔之首，此慶二也。

translations.literal: You's virtue is in yin; the first month establishes yin as natal day, combining with the month's virtue at the head of the New Year's first day—this is the second felicity.
translations.idiomatic: You's virtue is in yin; the first month establishes yin as natal day, combining with the month's virtue at New Year's head—this is the second felicity.

sentences.zh: 庚申之日，即是行年，乙德在庚，卯德在申，來年乙卯，是行年與歲合德，而在元旦之朝，此慶三也。

translations.literal: The day geng-shen is precisely the year of personal fortune; yi's virtue is in geng, mao's virtue in shen; next year yi-mao is the year of personal fortune combining with the year's virtue on New Year's morning—this is the third felicity.
translations.idiomatic: The day geng-shen is the year of personal fortune; next year yi-mao combines year-fortune with year-virtue on New Year's morning—this is the third felicity.

sentences.zh: 《陰陽書》雲：『年命與歲月合德者，必有福慶。』

translations.literal: The Book of Yin-Yang says, 'When natal fortune combines with year and month virtue, blessing must follow.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Yin-Yang says, 'When natal fortune combines with year and month virtue, blessing must follow.'

sentences.zh: 《洪範傳》雲：『歲之朝，月之朝，日之朝，主王者。』

translations.literal: The Tradition of the Great Plan says, 'The morning of year, month, and day belong to the king.'
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of the Great Plan says, 'The morning of year, month, and day belong to the king.'

sentences.zh: 經書並謂三長應之者，延年福吉。

translations.literal: The classics all say that when the three chiefs respond, life extends and fortune is auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The classics all say that when the three chiefs respond, life extends and fortune is auspicious.

sentences.zh: 況乃甲寅部首，十一月陽之始，朔旦冬至，是聖王上元。

translations.literal: Moreover, jia-yin is the head of the year; the eleventh month is the start of yang; the first day at the winter solstice is the sage king's upper origin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover jia-yin heads the year; the eleventh month starts yang; the first day at the winter solstice is the sage king's upper origin.

sentences.zh: 正月是正陽之月，歲之首，月之先。

translations.literal: The first month is the month of correct yang, the head of the year and foremost of months.
translations.idiomatic: The first month is the month of correct yang, head of the year and foremost of months.

sentences.zh: 朔旦是歲之元，月之朝，日之先，嘉辰之會。

translations.literal: The first day is the origin of the year, the morning of the month, the fore of the day—a meeting of auspicious seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The first day is the year's origin, the month's morning, the day's fore—a meeting of auspicious seasons.

sentences.zh: 而本命為九元之先，行年為三長之首，並與歲月合德。

translations.literal: Natal fortune is the fore of the nine origins; the year of personal fortune is the head of the three chiefs—both combine virtue with year and month.
translations.idiomatic: Natal fortune is the fore of the nine origins; the year of personal fortune heads the three chiefs—both combine virtue with year and month.

sentences.zh: 所以《靈寶經》雲：『角音龍精，其祚日強。』

translations.literal: Therefore the Classic of the Numinous Treasure says, 'The horn tone is dragon essence; its mandate grows daily stronger.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Classic of the Numinous Treasure says, 'The horn tone is dragon essence; its mandate grows daily stronger.'

sentences.zh: 來歲年命納音俱角，曆之與經，如合符契。

translations.literal: Next year's natal fortune and received tone are both horn; calendar and classic match like tally and seal.
translations.idiomatic: Next year's natal fortune and received tone are both horn; calendar and classic match like tally and seal.

sentences.zh: 又甲寅、乙卯，天地合也，甲寅之年，以辛酉冬至，來年乙卯，以甲子夏至。

translations.literal: Moreover jia-yin and yi-mao are Heaven-and-Earth combination: in the jia-yin year the winter solstice is xin-you; next year yi-mao the summer solstice is jia-zi.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover jia-yin and yi-mao combine Heaven and Earth: in jia-yin the winter solstice is xin-you; next year yi-mao the summer solstice is jia-zi.

sentences.zh: 冬至陽始，郊天之日，即是至尊本命，此慶四也。

translations.literal: The winter solstice is yang's beginning and the day of suburban sacrifice to Heaven—it is precisely Your Majesty's natal day; this is the fourth felicity.
translations.idiomatic: The winter solstice begins yang and is the day of sacrifice to Heaven—it is Your Majesty's natal day; this is the fourth felicity.

sentences.zh: 夏至陰始，祀地之辰，即是皇后本命，此慶五也。

translations.literal: The summer solstice is yin's beginning and the day of sacrifice to Earth—it is precisely the empress's natal day; this is the fifth felicity.
translations.idiomatic: The summer solstice begins yin and is the day of sacrifice to Earth—it is the empress's natal day; this is the fifth felicity.

sentences.zh: 至尊德並乾之覆育，皇后仁同地之載養，所以二儀元氣，並會本辰。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's virtue matches Heaven's covering nurture; the empress's benevolence matches Earth's bearing nurture—thus the two origins' primordial qi both meet at the natal days."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue matches Heaven's nurture; the empress's benevolence matches Earth's nurture—thus the two origins' qi meet at the natal days."

sentences.zh: 上覽之大悅，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: The emperor read it with great pleasure and granted five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it with great pleasure and granted five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 房陵王時為太子，言東宮多鬼巉，鼠妖數見。

translations.literal: Prince of Fangling was then crown prince; it was said the Eastern Palace had many ghostly precipices and rat demons appeared repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fangling was then crown prince; the Eastern Palace was said to have many ghosts and rat demons appeared repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 上令吉詣東宮，禳邪氣。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Ji to go to the Eastern Palace and exorcise evil qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ji to the Eastern Palace to exorcise evil qi.

sentences.zh: 于宣慈殿設神坐，有回風從艮地鬼門來，掃太子坐。

translations.literal: At Xuanci Hall he set up spirit seats; a whirlwind came from the northeast, the ghost gate of the gen position, sweeping the crown prince's seat.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanci Hall he set spirit seats; a whirlwind came from gen's ghost gate in the northeast, sweeping the crown prince's seat.

sentences.zh: 吉以桃湯葦火驅逐之，風出宮門而止。

translations.literal: Ji used peach broth and reed fire to drive it off; the wind went out the palace gate and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ji used peach broth and reed fire to drive it off; the wind went out the palace gate and stopped.

sentences.zh: 又謝土，於未地設壇，為四門，置五帝坐。

translations.literal: He also performed soil-thanking rites, setting an altar at the wei position with four gates and seats for the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: He also performed soil-thanking rites, setting an altar at wei with four gates and seats for the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 于時至寒，有楎蟆從西南來，入人門，升赤帝坐，還從人門而出。

translations.literal: It was then extreme cold; a toad came from the southwest, entered the human gate, ascended the Red Emperor's seat, and returned out the human gate.
translations.idiomatic: In extreme cold a toad came from the southwest, entered the human gate, ascended the Red Emperor's seat, and returned out the human gate.

sentences.zh: 行數步，忽然不見。

translations.literal: After going several paces it suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: After several paces it suddenly vanished.

sentences.zh: 上大異之，賞賜優洽。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly astonished and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly astonished and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 又上言太子當不安位，時上陰欲廢立，得其言是之。

translations.literal: He also said the crown prince would not securely hold his position; the emperor secretly wished to depose and install, and finding his words agreeable, valued them.
translations.idiomatic: He also said the crown prince would not hold his position securely; the emperor secretly wished to depose and install, and valued his words.

sentences.zh: 由此每被顧問。

translations.literal: From this he was frequently consulted.
translations.idiomatic: From this he was frequently consulted.

sentences.zh: 及獻皇后崩，上令吉卜擇葬所，吉曆筮山原，至一處，雲「卜年二千，卜世二百」，具圖而奏之。

translations.literal: When Empress Xian died, the emperor ordered Ji to divinely select the burial site; Ji divined mountains and plains until he reached one place and said, "Two thousand years of divination, two hundred generations of divination," drew a map, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xian died the emperor ordered Ji to select the burial site; Ji divined until one place yielded "two thousand years of divination, two hundred generations," drew a map, and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吉凶由人，不在於地。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Fortune and misfortune depend on men, not on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Fortune and misfortune depend on men, not on the ground.

sentences.zh: 高緯父葬，豈不卜乎？

translations.literal: When Gao Wei's father was buried, was it not divined?
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Wei's father was buried, was it not divined?

sentences.zh: 國尋滅亡。

translations.literal: The state was soon destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The state was soon destroyed.

sentences.zh: 正如我家墓田，若雲不吉，朕不當為天子；

translations.literal: Just like our family grave fields—if one said inauspicious, I should not have become Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Just like our family graves—if they were inauspicious, I should not have become Son of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 若雲不凶，我弟不當戰沒。」

translations.literal: if one said not inauspicious, my younger brother should not have died in battle."
translations.idiomatic: if not inauspicious, my brother should not have died in battle."

sentences.zh: 然竟從吉言。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he followed Ji's words.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he followed Ji's words.

sentences.zh: 吉表曰：「去月十六日，皇后山陵西北，雞未鳴前，有黑雲方圓五六百步，從地屬天。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized, "On the sixteenth of last month, northwest of the empress's tomb, before the cock crowed, black clouds square, five or six hundred paces, rose from earth to sky.
translations.idiomatic: Ji memorialized, "On the sixteenth of last month, northwest of the empress's tomb, before cockcrow, black clouds five or six hundred paces square rose from earth to sky.

sentences.zh: 東南又有旌旗車馬帳幕，佈滿七八裡，並有人往來檢校，部伍甚整，日出乃滅，同見者十餘人。

translations.literal: Southeastward were also banners, chariots, horses, and canopies filling seven or eight li, with people coming and going to inspect; the ranks were very orderly, vanishing at sunrise—more than ten people saw it together.
translations.idiomatic: Southeastward were banners, chariots, horses, and canopies filling seven or eight li, with people inspecting in orderly ranks, vanishing at sunrise—more than ten saw it.

sentences.zh: 謹案《葬書》雲：『氣王與姓相生，大吉。』

translations.literal: According to the Book of Burial: 'When the site's qi is king and generates the surname, great fortune.'
translations.idiomatic: According to the Book of Burial: 'When the site's qi is king and generates the surname, great fortune.'

sentences.zh: 今黑氣當冬王，與姓相生，是大吉利，子孫無疆之候也。」

translations.literal: Now the black qi is king in winter and generates the surname—greatly auspicious, a sign of boundless descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Now the black qi is king in winter and generates the surname—greatly auspicious, a sign of boundless descendants."

sentences.zh: 上大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 其後上將親臨發殯，吉複奏上曰：「至尊本命辛酉，今歲鬥魁及天岡，臨卯酉，謹按《陰陽書》，不得臨喪。」

translations.literal: Later when the emperor was about to attend the empress's funeral in person, Ji again memorialized, "Your Majesty's natal fortune is xin-you; this year the Dipper's handle and the celestial ridge face mao-you—according to the Book of Yin-Yang, one must not attend a funeral."
translations.idiomatic: Later when the emperor would attend the funeral in person, Ji memorialized, "Your Majesty's natal fortune is xin-you; this year the Dipper and celestial ridge face mao-you—by the Book of Yin-Yang one must not attend a funeral."

sentences.zh: 上不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 退而告族人蕭平仲曰：「皇太子遣宇文左率深謝餘雲：『公前稱我當為太子，竟有其驗，終不忘也。

translations.literal: Retiring, he told clansman Xiao Pingzhong, "The crown prince sent Yuwen, commander of the Left Guard, to thank me deeply: 'You said I would become crown prince; it proved true, and I shall never forget it.
translations.idiomatic: Retiring, he told clansman Xiao Pingzhong, "The crown prince sent Yuwen, commander of the Left Guard, to thank me deeply: 'You said I would become crown prince; it proved true, and I shall never forget it.

sentences.zh: 今卜山陵，務令我早立。

translations.literal: Now in divining the tomb, he wants me established early.
translations.idiomatic: Now in divining the tomb he wants me established early.

sentences.zh: 我立之後，當以富貴相報。』

translations.literal: When I am established, I shall repay you with wealth and honor.'
translations.idiomatic: When I am established, I shall repay you with wealth and honor.'

sentences.zh: 吾記之曰：『後四載，太子禦天下。』

translations.literal: I recorded it, saying, 'After four years, the crown prince will rule the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: I recorded it, saying, 'After four years, the crown prince will rule the realm.'

sentences.zh: 今山陵氣應，上又臨喪，兆益見矣。

translations.literal: Now the tomb's qi responds; the emperor attends the funeral—the omen grows clearer.
translations.idiomatic: Now the tomb's qi responds; the emperor attends the funeral—the omen grows clearer.

sentences.zh: 且太子得政，隋其亡乎！

translations.literal: When the crown prince takes power, will Sui not perish!
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince takes power, will Sui not perish!

sentences.zh: 當有真人出治之矣。

translations.literal: A true man will arise to govern.
translations.idiomatic: A true man will arise to govern.

sentences.zh: 吾前紿雲卜年二千者，是三十字也；

translations.literal: My earlier deception that divination was two thousand years meant thirty characters;
translations.idiomatic: My earlier deception that divination was two thousand years meant thirty characters;

sentences.zh: 卜世二百者，取三十二運也。

translations.literal: divination of two hundred generations took thirty-two cycles.
translations.idiomatic: divination of two hundred generations took thirty-two cycles.

sentences.zh: 吾言信矣，汝其志之。」

translations.literal: My words are verified—remember them."
translations.idiomatic: My words are verified—remember them."

sentences.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，拜太府少卿，加位開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Ji was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury with the added rank of Grand Master with the Opening of an Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Ji was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury with the added rank of Grand Master with the Opening of an Office.

sentences.zh: 嘗行經華陰，見楊素塚上有白氣屬天，密言於帝。

translations.literal: Once passing Huayin he saw white qi from Yang Su's tomb reaching to Heaven and secretly told the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Huayin he saw white qi from Yang Su's tomb reaching heaven and secretly told the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，吉曰：「其候素家當有兵禍，滅門之象。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; Ji said, "The sign is that Su's house will suffer military calamity—a sign of extermination of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; Ji said, "The sign is military calamity for Su's house—extermination of the clan.

sentences.zh: 改葬者，庶可免乎！」

translations.literal: If the tomb is moved, perhaps this can be avoided!"
translations.idiomatic: If the tomb is moved, perhaps this can be avoided!"

sentences.zh: 帝后從容謂楊玄感曰：「公家宜早改葬。」

translations.literal: The emperor later told Yang Xuangan at leisure, "Your family should move the tomb soon."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later told Yang Xuangan at leisure, "Your family should move the tomb soon."

sentences.zh: 玄感亦微知其故，以為吉祥，托以遼東未滅，不遑私門之事。

translations.literal: Xuangan also faintly knew the reason and, thinking it auspicious, pleaded that Liaodong was not yet pacified and he had no leisure for private family matters.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan faintly knew the reason, thought it auspicious, and pleaded Liaodong was not yet pacified and he had no leisure for family matters.

sentences.zh: 未幾而玄感以反族滅，帝彌信之。

translations.literal: Before long Xuangan rebelled and his clan was exterminated; the emperor trusted Ji all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xuangan rebelled and his clan was exterminated; the emperor trusted Ji all the more.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，卒官。

translations.literal: More than a year later he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 著《金海》三十卷，《相經要錄》一卷，《宅經》八卷，《葬經》六卷，《樂譜》二十卷及《帝王養生方》二卷，《相手版要決》一卷，《太一立成》一卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He authored Golden Sea in thirty scrolls, Essentials of Physiognomy in one scroll, Dwelling Classic in eight scrolls, Burial Classic in six scrolls, Music Treatise in twenty scrolls, and Methods for Nourishing the Emperor in two scrolls, Essentials for Reading Hand Tablets in one scroll, and Establishment of the Grand One in one scroll—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Golden Sea in 30 scrolls, Essentials of Physiognomy in 1 scroll, Dwelling Classic in 8 scrolls, Burial Classic in 6 scrolls, Music Treatise in 20 scrolls, Methods for Nourishing the Emperor in 2 scrolls, Essentials for Reading Hand Tablets in 1 scroll, and Establishment of the Grand One in 1 scroll—all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 時有楊伯醜，臨孝恭、劉祐，俱以陰陽術數知名。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Bochou, Lin Xiaogong, and Liu You were all famed for yin-yang and numerology.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Bochou, Lin Xiaogong, and Liu You were all famed for yin-yang and numerology.

sentences.zh: 楊伯醜，馮翊武鄉人也。

translations.literal: Yang Bochou was a man of Wuxiang in Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bochou came from Wuxiang in Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 好讀《易》，隱于華山。

translations.literal: He loved to read the Changes and hid on Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Changes and withdrew to Mount Hua.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，被徵入朝，見公卿不為禮，無貴賤皆汝之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was summoned to court; seeing dukes and ministers he made no courtesy, addressing all regardless of rank as "you."
translations.idiomatic: At Kaihuang's start he was summoned to court; he made no courtesy to dukes and ministers, addressing all as "you."

sentences.zh: 人不能測也。

translations.literal: People could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: People could not fathom him.

sentences.zh: 高祖召與語，竟無所答。

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned him to speak; in the end he answered nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned him to speak; he answered nothing.

sentences.zh: 上賜之衣服，至朝堂，舍之而去。

translations.literal: The emperor granted him clothes; at the court hall he cast them off and left.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted clothes; at court he cast them off and left.

sentences.zh: 於是被發陽狂，遊行市里，形體垢穢，未嘗櫛沐。

translations.literal: Thereafter he let his hair hang loose in feigned madness, wandering the market streets, his body filthy, never combing or bathing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he feigned madness with loose hair, wandering the markets filthy, never combing or bathing.

sentences.zh: 嘗有張永樂者，賣卜京師，伯醜每從之遊。

translations.literal: Once there was a Zhang Yongle who sold divination in the capital; Bochou often wandered with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongle sold divination in the capital; Bochou often wandered with him.

sentences.zh: 永樂為卦有不能決者，伯醜輒為分析爻象，尋幽入微。

translations.literal: When Yongle's hexagrams had points he could not decide, Bochou would analyze the lines and images, probing the subtle and entering the minute.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongle could not decide a hexagram, Bochou analyzed the lines, probing the subtle.

sentences.zh: 永樂嗟服，自以為非所及也。

translations.literal: Yongle sighed in admiration, feeling himself unable to match.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle sighed in admiration, feeling himself unable to match.

sentences.zh: 伯醜亦開肆賣卜。

translations.literal: Bochou also opened a shop selling divination.
translations.idiomatic: Bochou also opened a divination shop.

sentences.zh: 有人嘗失子，就伯醜筮者。

translations.literal: Once someone had lost a child and came to Bochou for divination.
translations.idiomatic: Once someone lost a child and came to Bochou for divination.

sentences.zh: 卦成，伯醜曰：「汝子在懷遠坊南門道東北壁上，有青裙女子抱之，可往取也。」

translations.literal: When the hexagram was complete Bochou said, "Your child is on the northeast wall of the south gate road in Huaiyuan Ward, held by a woman in a green skirt—you may go fetch him."
translations.idiomatic: When the hexagram was done Bochou said, "Your child is on the northeast wall of the south gate road in Huaiyuan Ward, held by a woman in a green skirt—go fetch him."

sentences.zh: 如言果得。

translations.literal: It was exactly as he said and the child was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: It was exactly as he said and the child was recovered.

sentences.zh: 或者有金數兩，夫妻共藏之，于後失金，其夫意妻有異志，將逐之。

translations.literal: Another case: a couple had hidden several taels of gold; later the gold was lost and the husband suspected the wife of unfaithful intent and was about to drive her out.
translations.idiomatic: A couple hid several taels of gold; later it was lost and the husband suspected the wife and was about to drive her out.

sentences.zh: 其妻稱冤，以詣伯醜，為筮之曰：「金在矣。」

translations.literal: The wife proclaimed her innocence and went to Bochou, who divined and said, "The gold is still here."
translations.idiomatic: The wife proclaimed innocence and went to Bochou, who divined, "The gold is still here."

sentences.zh: 悉呼其家人，指一人曰：「可取金來！」

translations.literal: He called all the household and pointed to one person, saying, "Go fetch the gold!"
translations.idiomatic: He called the household and pointed to one, saying, "Go fetch the gold!"

sentences.zh: 其人赧然，應聲而取之。

translations.literal: That person flushed and at the word retrieved it.
translations.idiomatic: That person flushed and retrieved it at the word.

sentences.zh: 道士韋知常詣伯醜問吉凶，伯醜曰：「汝勿東北行，必不得已，當早還。

translations.literal: The Daoist Wei Zhichang came to Bochou to ask fortune; Bochou said, "Do not go northeast; if you must, return early.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist Wei Zhichang asked Bochou about fortune; Bochou said, "Do not go northeast; if you must, return early.

sentences.zh: 不然者，楊素斬汝頭。」

translations.literal: Otherwise Yang Su will cut off your head."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Yang Su will cut off your head."

sentences.zh: 未幾，上令知常事漢王諒。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor ordered Zhichang to serve Prince Xiu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor ordered Zhichang to serve Prince Xiu of Han.

sentences.zh: 俄而上崩，諒舉兵反，知常逃歸京師。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor died; Prince Xiu rebelled and Zhichang fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor died; Prince Xiu rebelled and Zhichang fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 知常先與楊素有隙，及素平并州，先訪知常，將斬之，賴此獲免。

translations.literal: Zhichang had earlier had a rift with Yang Su; when Su pacified Bingzhou he first sought Zhichang to behead him—only by this was he spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichang had a rift with Yang Su; when Su pacified Bingzhou he sought Zhichang to behead him—only by this was he spared.

sentences.zh: 又人有失馬，來詣伯醜卜者。

translations.literal: Another man had lost a horse and came to Bochou for divination.
translations.idiomatic: Another man lost a horse and came to Bochou for divination.

sentences.zh: 時伯醜為皇太子所召，在途遇之，立為作卦，卦成，曰：「我不遑為卿占之，卿且向西市東壁門南第三店，為我買魚作膾，當得馬矣。」

translations.literal: Bochou was then summoned by the crown prince; on the road he met the man, stopped to make a hexagram, and when complete said, "I have no leisure to divined for you—go to the third shop south of the east wall gate of the west market, buy fish and make kuai for me, and you will get your horse."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned by the crown prince, Bochou met the man on the road, made a hexagram, and said, "I have no leisure—go to the third shop south of the west market's east wall gate, buy fish kuai for me, and you will get your horse."

sentences.zh: 其人如此言，須臾，有一人牽所失馬而至，遂擒之。

translations.literal: The man did as told; before long someone leading the lost horse came and he seized it.
translations.idiomatic: The man did so; before long someone leading the lost horse came and he seized it.

sentences.zh: 崖州嘗獻徑寸珠，其使者陰易之，上心疑焉，召伯醜令筮。

translations.literal: Ya Prefecture once presented a pearl an inch in diameter; the envoy secretly exchanged it and the emperor's heart was suspicious; he summoned Bochou to divined.
translations.idiomatic: Ya Prefecture once presented an inch-pearl; the envoy secretly exchanged it and the emperor was suspicious; he summoned Bochou to divined.

sentences.zh: 伯醜曰：「有物出自水中，質圓而色光，是大珠也。

translations.literal: Bochou said, "There is an object from the water, round and bright in color—it is a great pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Bochou said, "An object from the water, round and bright—it is a great pearl.

sentences.zh: 今為人所隱。」

translations.literal: Now it is hidden by someone."
translations.idiomatic: Now someone has hidden it."

sentences.zh: 具言隱者姓名容狀。

translations.literal: He fully stated the hider's name and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He fully stated the hider's name and appearance.

sentences.zh: 上如言簿責之，果得本珠。

translations.literal: The emperor checked the register as stated and indeed recovered the original pearl.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor checked the register as stated and recovered the original pearl.

sentences.zh: 上奇之，賜帛二十匹。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled and granted twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and granted twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒何妥嘗詣之論《易》，聞妥之言，倏然而笑曰：「何用鄭玄、王弼之言乎！」

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Academy He Tuo once came to discuss the Changes with him; hearing Tuo's words Bochou suddenly laughed and said, "What use are the words of Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi!"
translations.idiomatic: Academy Director He Tuo came to discuss the Changes; hearing Tuo, Bochou laughed, "What use are Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi!"

sentences.zh: 久之，微有辨答，所說辭義，皆異先儒之旨，而思理玄妙，故論者以為天然獨得，非常人所及也。

translations.literal: After a long while he offered slight replies; what he said in meaning differed from earlier Confucians' intent, yet his reasoning was abstruse and marvelous—discussants considered him naturally unique, not within ordinary reach.
translations.idiomatic: After long while he offered slight replies differing from earlier Confucians yet abstruse and marvelous—discussants considered him naturally unique.

sentences.zh: 竟以壽終。

translations.literal: In the end he died at full span of years.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he died at full span of years.

sentences.zh: 臨孝恭，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Lin Xiaogong was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xiaogong came from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 明天文算術，高祖甚親遇之。

translations.literal: He understood astronomy and calculation; Gaozu treated him with great personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: He understood astronomy and calculation; Gaozu treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 每言災祥之事，未嘗不中，上因令考定陰陽。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of calamities and auspicious signs, he never missed; the emperor therefore ordered him to examine and fix yin-yang.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of omens he never missed; the emperor ordered him to examine yin-yang.

sentences.zh: 官至上儀同。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Senior Grand Master of State with the Three Excellencies' Honors.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Senior Grand Master of State with the Three Excellencies' Honors.

sentences.zh: 著《欹器圖》三卷，《地動銅儀經》一卷，《九宮五墓》一卷，《遁甲月令》十卷，《元辰經》十卷，《元辰厄》一百九卷，《百怪書》十八卷，《祿命書》二十卷，《九宮龜經》一百一十卷，《太一式經》三十卷，《孔子馬頭易卜書》一卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He authored Tilt-Vessel Diagram in three scrolls, Treatise on the Earthquake Bronze Instrument in one scroll, Nine Palaces Five Tombs in one scroll, Hidden Armor Monthly Commands in ten scrolls, Primordial Cycle Classic in ten scrolls, Primordial Cycle Calamity in one hundred nine scrolls, Book of a Hundred Marvels in eighteen scrolls, Salary-and-Fate Book in twenty scrolls, Nine Palaces Tortoise Classic in one hundred ten scrolls, Grand One Style Classic in thirty scrolls, and Confucius Horse-Head Changes Divination Book in one scroll—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Tilt-Vessel Diagram in 3 scrolls, Treatise on the Earthquake Bronze Instrument in 1 scroll, Nine Palaces Five Tombs in 1 scroll, Hidden Armor Monthly Commands in 10 scrolls, Primordial Cycle Classic in 10 scrolls, Primordial Cycle Calamity in 109 scrolls, Book of a Hundred Marvels in 18 scrolls, Salary-and-Fate Book in 20 scrolls, Nine Palaces Tortoise Classic in 110 scrolls, Grand One Style Classic in 30 scrolls, and Confucius Horse-Head Changes Divination Book in 1 scroll—all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 劉祐，滎陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu You was a man of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu You came from Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，為大都督，封索盧縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he served as Grand Commander and was enfeoffed as Duke of Suolu County.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaihuang's start he served as Grand Commander and was enfeoffed Duke of Suolu County.

sentences.zh: 其所占候，合如符契，高祖甚親之。

translations.literal: His prognostications matched like tally and seal; Gaozu was very close to him.
translations.idiomatic: His prognostications matched like tally and seal; Gaozu was very close to him.

sentences.zh: 初與張賓、劉暉、馬顯定曆。

translations.literal: At first together with Zhang Bin, Liu Hui, and Ma Xian he fixed the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: At first with Zhang Bin, Liu Hui, and Ma Xian he fixed the calendar.

sentences.zh: 後奉詔撰兵書十卷，名曰《金韜》，上善之。

translations.literal: Later by imperial edict he compiled a military book in ten scrolls called Golden Sheath; the emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Later by edict he compiled a military book in ten scrolls called Golden Sheath; the emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 複著《陰策》二十卷，《觀台飛候》六卷，《玄象要記》五卷，《律曆術文》一卷，《婚姻志》三卷，《產乳志》二卷，《式經》四卷，《四時立成法》一卷，《安曆志》十二卷，《歸正易》十卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He also authored Hidden Stratagem in twenty scrolls, Observation Platform Flying Prognostics in six scrolls, Essentials of the Dark Signs in five scrolls, Treatise on Pitch and Calendar in one scroll, Marriage Records in three scrolls, Childbirth Records in two scrolls, Style Classic in four scrolls, Four Seasons Establishment Method in one scroll, Pacifying Calendar Records in twelve scrolls, and Return-to-Correctness Changes in ten scrolls—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also authored Hidden Stratagem in 20 scrolls, Observation Platform Flying Prognostics in 6 scrolls, Essentials of the Dark Signs in 5 scrolls, Treatise on Pitch and Calendar in 1 scroll, Marriage Records in 3 scrolls, Childbirth Records in 2 scrolls, Style Classic in 4 scrolls, Four Seasons Establishment Method in 1 scroll, Pacifying Calendar Records in 12 scrolls, and Return-to-Correctness Changes in 10 scrolls—all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄，渤海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan Zhang Zhouxuan was a man of Su in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan came from Su in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 博學多通，尤精術數。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and mastered many fields, especially numerology.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and mastered many fields, especially numerology.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史趙煚薦之，高祖征授雲騎尉，直太史，參議律曆事。

translations.literal: Governor Zhao Shuang of Ji Prefecture recommended him; Gaozu summoned and appointed him Cloud Cavalry Captain, serving directly in the Astrologer's Office to discuss law and calendar affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhao Shuang of Ji recommended him; Gaozu summoned him as Cloud Cavalry Captain in the Astrologer's Office to discuss law and calendar.

sentences.zh: 時輩多出其下，由是太史令劉暉等甚忌之。

translations.literal: Contemporaries mostly ranked below him; therefore Grand Astrologer Liu Hui and others greatly envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mostly ranked below him; Grand Astrologer Liu Hui and others greatly envied him.

sentences.zh: 然暉言多不中，胄玄所推步甚精密，上異之。

translations.literal: Yet Hui's words often missed, while Zhouxuan's calculations were very precise; the emperor was impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hui often missed while Zhouxuan's calculations were precise; the emperor was impressed.

sentences.zh: 令楊素與術數人立議六十一事，皆舊法久難通者，令暉與胄玄等辯析之。

translations.literal: He ordered Yang Su and numerologists to establish discussion on sixty-one points—all old methods long hard to apply—and had Hui and Zhouxuan debate and analyze them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Su and numerologists to debate sixty-one points—all old methods long hard to apply—having Hui and Zhouxuan analyze them.

sentences.zh: 暉杜口一無所答，胄玄通者五十四焉。

translations.literal: Hui shut his mouth and answered nothing; Zhouxuan mastered fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Hui shut his mouth and answered nothing; Zhouxuan mastered fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 由是擢拜員外散騎侍郎，兼太史令，賜物千段，暉及黨與八人皆斥逐之。

translations.literal: On that account he was promoted to Extraordinary Regular Attendant and concurrently Grand Astrologer, granted a thousand bolts of goods; Hui and his faction of eight were all expelled.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Extraordinary Regular Attendant and concurrently Grand Astrologer, granted a thousand bolts; Hui and his faction of eight were expelled.

sentences.zh: 改定新曆，言前曆差一日，內史通事顏敏楚上言曰：「漢時落下閎改《顓頊曆》作《太初曆》，雲後當差一日。

translations.literal: He revised the new calendar, saying the prior calendar was off by one day; Palace Clerk Yan Minchu submitted saying, "In Han, Luoxia Hong revised the Zhuanxu Calendar into the Taichu Calendar, saying that after eight hundred years a sage would fix it.
translations.idiomatic: He revised the new calendar, saying the prior calendar was off one day; Clerk Yan Minchu submitted, "In Han Luoxia Hong revised the Zhuanxu Calendar into the Taichu Calendar, saying that after eight hundred years a sage would fix it.

sentences.zh: 八百年當有聖者定之。

translations.literal: After eight hundred years there should be a sage to fix it.
translations.idiomatic: After eight hundred years a sage should fix it.

sentences.zh: 計今相去七百一十年，術者舉其成數，聖者之謂，其在今乎！」

translations.literal: Counting from then to now is seven hundred ten years; numerologists cite the round number—the sage's meaning—is it not in the present!"
translations.idiomatic: Counting from then is seven hundred ten years; numerologists cite the round number—the sage's meaning—is it not now!"

sentences.zh: 上大悅，漸見親用。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and gradually saw him used closely.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and gradually used him closely.

sentences.zh: 胄玄所為曆法，與古不同者有三事：

translations.literal: Zhouxuan's calendar method differed from antiquity in three matters:
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan's calendar differed from antiquity in three matters:

sentences.zh: 其一，宋祖沖之于歲周之末，創設差分，冬至漸移，不循舊軌。

translations.literal: First: Song's Zu Chongzhi at the end of the year cycle created differential parts; the winter solstice gradually shifted and did not follow the old track.
translations.idiomatic: First: Song's Zu Chongzhi at the year cycle's end created differential parts; the winter solstice gradually shifted off the old track.

sentences.zh: 每四十六年，卻差一度。

translations.literal: Every forty-six years it retreated one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Every forty-six years it retreated one degree.

sentences.zh: 至梁虞𠠎曆法，嫌沖之所差太多，因以一百八十六年冬至移一度。

translations.literal: To Liang's Yu Xiao's calendar method, Xiao thought Chongzhi's difference too great and therefore made the winter solstice shift one degree every one hundred eighty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Yu Xiao's calendar, Xiao thought Chongzhi's difference too great and made the winter solstice shift one degree every 186 years.

sentences.zh: 胄玄以此二術，年限懸隔，追檢古注，所失極多，遂折中兩家，以為度法。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan considered these two methods too far apart in years; checking ancient commentaries, the errors were extremely many; he therefore split the difference between the two houses as degree method.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan found these methods too far apart; checking ancient commentaries the errors were many; he split the difference as degree method.

sentences.zh: 冬至所宿，歲別漸移，八十三年卻行一度，則上合堯時日永星火，次符漢曆宿起牛初。

translations.literal: The lodge occupied at the winter solstice gradually shifts from year to year; if it retreats one degree every eighty-three years, then above it accords with Yao's time, when the days were long and the Fire Star was at culmination, and next it matches the Han calendar, whose lodges began at the start of Ox.
translations.idiomatic: The lodge occupied at the winter solstice gradually shifts from year to year; if it retreats one degree every eighty-three years, then above it accords with Yao's time, when the days were long and the Fire Star was at culmination, and next it matches the Han calendar, whose lodges began at the start of Ox.

sentences.zh: 明其前後，並皆密當。

translations.literal: Before and after, all were closely fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after, all closely fit.

sentences.zh: 其二，周馬顯造《丙寅元曆》，有陰陽轉法，加減章分，進退蝕餘，乃推定日，創開此數。

translations.literal: Second: Zhou's Ma Xian created the Bingyin Origin Calendar with yin-yang rotation method, adding and subtracting chapter parts, advancing and retreating eclipse remainder—thus deducing fixed days and opening this number.
translations.idiomatic: Second: Zhou's Ma Xian created the Bingyin Origin Calendar with yin-yang rotation, adding and subtracting chapter parts, advancing and retreating eclipse remainder—deducing fixed days.

sentences.zh: 當時術者，多不能曉。

translations.literal: Numerologists of the time mostly could not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Numerologists of the time mostly could not understand.

sentences.zh: 張賓因而用之，莫能考正。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin therefore used it but could not examine and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin used it but could not examine and correct.

sentences.zh: 胄玄以為加時先後，逐氣參差，就月為斷，於理未可。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan considered that adding the hour first and last, following qi with disparity, taking the month as cutoff—in principle this would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan considered adding the hour first and last by qi disparity with month as cutoff—in principle wrong.

sentences.zh: 乃因二十四氣列其盈縮所出，實由日行遲則月逐日易及，令合朔加時早，日行速則月逐日少遲，令合朔加時晚。

translations.literal: He therefore listed the surplus and deficit of each of the twenty-four qi, showing that when the sun's motion is slow the moon daily easily catches up, making new moon's added hour early; when the sun's motion is fast the moon daily lags slightly, making new moon's added hour late.
translations.idiomatic: He listed surplus and deficit of each of the twenty-four qi: when the sun is slow the moon catches up daily, making new moon early; when fast the moon lags, making new moon late.

sentences.zh: 檢前代加時早晚，以為損益之率。

translations.literal: Checking prior generations' early and late added hours, he made them the rates of increase and decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Checking prior generations' early and late added hours he made rates of increase and decrease.

sentences.zh: 日行自秋分已後至春分，其勢速，計一百八十二日而行一百八十度。

translations.literal: From after the autumn equinox to the spring equinox the sun's motion is fast—in one hundred eighty-two days it travels one hundred eighty degrees.
translations.idiomatic: From after the autumn equinox to the spring equinox the sun is fast—in 182 days it travels 180 degrees.

sentences.zh: 自春分已後至秋分，日行遲，計一百八十二日而行一百七十六度。

translations.literal: From after the spring equinox to the autumn equinox, the sun travels slowly: over one hundred eighty-two days it moves one hundred seventy-six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: From after the spring equinox to the autumn equinox, the sun travels slowly: over one hundred eighty-two days it moves one hundred seventy-six degrees.

sentences.zh: 每氣之下，即其率也。

translations.literal: Below each qi is its rate.
translations.idiomatic: Below each qi is its rate.

sentences.zh: 其三，自古諸曆，朔望值交，不問內外，入限便食。

translations.literal: Third: In all ancient calendars, when new and full moon met crossing, regardless of inner or outer limit, entering the limit meant eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Third: In ancient calendars when new and full moon met crossing, regardless of inner or outer limit, entering the limit meant eclipse.

sentences.zh: 張賓立法，創有外限，應食不食，猶未能明。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's method created an outer limit—when eclipse should occur it did not—yet this was still not clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin created an outer limit—when eclipse should occur it did not—yet still unclear.

sentences.zh: 胄玄以日行黃道，歲一周天，月行月道，二十七日有餘一周天。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan considered that the sun travels the Yellow Path, completing heaven in a year; the moon travels the moon path, completing heaven in twenty-seven-plus days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan considered the sun travels the Yellow Path yearly; the moon the moon path in 27-plus days.

sentences.zh: 月道交絡黃道，每行黃道內十三日有奇而出，又行黃道外十三日有奇而入，終而複始，月經黃道，謂之交，朔望去交前後各十五度已下，即為當食。

translations.literal: The moon path crosses the Yellow Path; every time it travels within the Yellow Path for thirteen-plus days it exits, then outside for thirteen-plus days it enters, ending and beginning again; when the moon crosses the Yellow Path it is called crossing; when new and full moon are within fifteen degrees before and after crossing, that is when eclipse should occur.
translations.idiomatic: The moon path crosses the Yellow Path; within for 13-plus days then out, outside for 13-plus days then in; when new and full moon are within 15 degrees of crossing, eclipse should occur.

sentences.zh: 若月行內道，則在黃道之北，食多有驗。

translations.literal: If the moon travels the inner path it is north of the Yellow Path and eclipses mostly verify.
translations.idiomatic: If the moon travels the inner path north of the Yellow Path, eclipses mostly verify.

sentences.zh: 月行外道，在黃道之南也，雖遇正交，無由掩映，食多不驗。

translations.literal: If the moon travels the outer path south of the Yellow Path, even meeting exact crossing there is no covering shadow and eclipses mostly do not verify.
translations.idiomatic: On the outer path south of the Yellow Path, even at exact crossing there is no shadow and eclipses mostly fail.

sentences.zh: 遂因前法，別立定限，隨交遠近，逐氣求差，損益食分，事皆明著。

translations.literal: He therefore followed the prior method, separately establishing fixed limits, following crossing distance and seeking disparity by qi, increasing and decreasing eclipse parts—all matters clearly shown.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the prior method, establishing fixed limits by crossing distance and qi disparity, increasing and decreasing eclipse parts—all clearly shown.

sentences.zh: 其超古獨異者有七事：

translations.literal: What surpassed antiquity and was uniquely different had seven matters:
translations.idiomatic: What surpassed antiquity had seven unique matters:

sentences.zh: 其一，古曆五星行度皆守恆率，見伏盈縮，悉無格准。

translations.literal: First: Ancient calendars' five planets' motion degrees all kept constant rates; appearance, hiding, surplus, and deficit had no standard frame.
translations.idiomatic: First: Ancient calendars kept constant rates for the five planets; appearance, hiding, surplus, and deficit had no standard.

sentences.zh: 胄玄推之，各得其真率，合見之數，與古不同。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan deduced them and each obtained its true rate; combined appearance numbers differed from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan deduced each true rate; combined appearance numbers differed from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其差多者，至加減三十許日。

translations.literal: The greatest differences reached adding and subtracting some thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest differences reached adding and subtracting some 30 days.

sentences.zh: 即如熒惑平見在雨水氣，即均加二十九日，見在小雪氣，則均減二十五日。

translations.literal: For example Mars at mean appearance in Rain Water qi uniformly add twenty-nine days; at appearance in Minor Snow qi uniformly subtract twenty-five days.
translations.idiomatic: For example Mars at mean appearance in Rain Water uniformly add 29 days; at Minor Snow subtract 25 days.

sentences.zh: 雖減平見，以為定見。

translations.literal: Though subtracting mean appearance to make fixed appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Though subtracting mean appearance to make fixed appearance.

sentences.zh: 諸星各有盈縮之數，皆如此例，但差數不同。

translations.literal: Each star had its surplus and deficit numbers—all such examples, but difference numbers differed.
translations.idiomatic: Each star had surplus and deficit numbers—all such examples, but numbers differed.

sentences.zh: 特其積候所知，時人不能原其意旨。

translations.literal: Only accumulated observations known—people of the time could not trace the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Only accumulated observations were known—contemporaries could not trace the intent.

sentences.zh: 其二，辰星舊率，一終再見，凡諸古曆，皆以為然，應見不見，人未能測。

translations.literal: Second: Mercury's old rate—one cycle, two appearances; all ancient calendars considered it so; when it should appear it did not—people could not measure.
translations.idiomatic: Second: Mercury's old rate—one cycle, two appearances; ancient calendars all assumed this; when it should appear it did not—people could not measure.

sentences.zh: 胄玄積候，知辰星一終之中，有時一見，及同類感召，相隨而出。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan's accumulated observations knew that within one Mercury cycle sometimes there was one appearance; and by kindred sympathetic response, following out together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan's observations knew that within one Mercury cycle sometimes there was one appearance; and by sympathetic response, following out together.

sentences.zh: 即如辰星平晨見在雨水氣者，應見即不見，若平晨見在啟蟄氣者，去日十八度外，三十六度內，晨有木火土金一星者，亦相隨見。

translations.literal: For example when Mercury at mean morning appearance in Rain Water qi should appear but does not; if at mean morning appearance in Awakening of Insects qi, beyond eighteen degrees from the sun and within thirty-six degrees, if morning has Wood, Fire, Earth, or Metal star, they also appear together.
translations.idiomatic: For example when Mercury at mean morning appearance in Rain Water should appear but does not; if at Awakening of Insects, beyond 18 degrees from the sun and within 36, if morning has Wood, Fire, Earth, or Metal star, they also appear together.

sentences.zh: 其三，古曆步術，行有定限，自見已後，依率而推。

translations.literal: Third: Ancient calendar step methods had fixed limits for motion; after appearance, deduce by rate.
translations.idiomatic: Third: Ancient step methods had fixed motion limits; after appearance, deduce by rate.

sentences.zh: 進退之期，莫知多少。

translations.literal: Periods of advance and retreat—none knew how many.
translations.idiomatic: Periods of advance and retreat—none knew how many.

sentences.zh: 胄玄積候，知五星遲速留退真數皆與古法不同，多者至差八十餘日，留回所在亦差八十餘度。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan's accumulated observations knew the five planets' slow, fast, stationary, and retreat true numbers all differed from ancient methods—most reaching differences of eighty-plus days; stationary and retrograde positions also differed eighty-plus degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan's observations knew the five planets' slow, fast, stationary, and retreat true numbers differed from ancient methods—most reaching 80-plus days; stationary and retrograde positions differed 80-plus degrees.

sentences.zh: 即如熒惑前疾初見在立冬初，則二百五十日行一百七十七度，定見在夏至初，則一百七十日行九十二度。

translations.literal: For example, if Mars in its earlier swift motion first appears at the beginning of Winter Establishment, then over two hundred fifty days it travels one hundred seventy-seven degrees; if its fixed appearance is at the beginning of Summer Solstice, then over one hundred seventy days it travels ninety-two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: For example, if Mars in its earlier swift motion first appears at the beginning of Winter Establishment, then over two hundred fifty days it travels one hundred seventy-seven degrees; if its fixed appearance is at the beginning of Summer Solstice, then over one hundred seventy days it travels ninety-two degrees.

sentences.zh: 追步天驗，今古皆密。

translations.literal: Checking against heaven's verification, ancient and modern both are close.
translations.idiomatic: Checking against heaven, ancient and modern both closely fit.

sentences.zh: 其四，古曆食分，依平即用，推驗多少，實數罕符。

translations.literal: Fourth: Ancient calendar eclipse parts used mean values directly; checking verification, actual numbers rarely matched.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Ancient eclipse parts used mean values; verification rarely matched.

sentences.zh: 胄玄積候，知月從木、火、土、金四星行有向背。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan's accumulated observations knew that when the moon follows Wood, Fire, Earth, or Metal stars there is facing and backing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan's observations knew when the moon follows Wood, Fire, Earth, or Metal stars there is facing and backing.

sentences.zh: 月向四星即速，背之則遲，皆十五度外，乃循本率。

translations.literal: When the moon faces the four stars it is fast; when backing it is slow—only beyond fifteen degrees does it follow the original rate.
translations.idiomatic: When facing the four stars the moon is fast; when backing slow—only beyond 15 degrees does it follow the original rate.

sentences.zh: 遂於交分，限其多少。

translations.literal: He therefore at crossing parts limited the amount.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore at crossing parts limited the amount.

sentences.zh: 其五，古曆加時，朔望同術。

translations.literal: Fifth: Ancient calendar added hours—new and full moon same method.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: Ancient added hours—new and full moon same method.

sentences.zh: 胄玄積候，知日食所在，隨方改變，傍正高下，每處不同。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan's accumulated observations knew solar eclipse location changes by region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan's observations knew solar eclipse location changes by region.

sentences.zh: 交有淺深，遲速亦異，約時立差，皆會天象。

translations.literal: Side, direct, high, and low differ at each place; crossing has shallow and deep, slow and fast also differ—approximate time establishes disparity, all matching celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: Side, direct, high, and low differ; crossing shallow and deep, slow and fast differ—approximate time establishes disparity, all matching signs.

sentences.zh: 其六，古曆交分即為食數，去交十四度者食一分，去交十三度食二分，去交十度食三分。

translations.literal: Sixth: Ancient calendar crossing parts were eclipse numbers: fourteen degrees from crossing eats one part, thirteen degrees two parts, ten degrees three parts.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: Ancient crossing parts were eclipse numbers: 14 degrees from crossing eats one part, 13 degrees two parts, 10 degrees three parts.

sentences.zh: 每近一度，食益一分，當交即食既。

translations.literal: Each nearer one degree the eclipse increases one part; at exact crossing it is total eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Each nearer one degree the eclipse increases one part; at exact crossing total eclipse.

sentences.zh: 其應少反多，應多反少，自古諸曆，未悉其原。

translations.literal: When less should be more and more should be less—ancient calendars did not know the source.
translations.idiomatic: When less should be more and more less—ancient calendars did not know the source.

sentences.zh: 胄玄積候，知當交之中，月掩日不能畢盡，其食反少，去交五六時，月在日內，掩日便盡，故食乃既。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan knew at exact crossing the moon cannot completely cover the sun—eclipse is less; at five or six degrees when the moon is within the sun, covering completely, eclipse is total.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan knew at exact crossing the moon cannot completely cover the sun—eclipse is less; at five or six degrees when the moon is within the sun, covering completely, eclipse is total.

sentences.zh: 自此已後，更遠者其食又少。

translations.literal: From this onward, farther ones have less eclipse again.
translations.idiomatic: Farther ones have less eclipse again.

sentences.zh: 交之前後在冬至皆爾。

translations.literal: Before and after crossing at winter solstice are all thus.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after crossing at winter solstice are all thus.

sentences.zh: 若近夏至，其率又差。

translations.literal: If near summer solstice the rates differ again.
translations.idiomatic: Near summer solstice the rates differ again.

sentences.zh: 所立食分，最為詳密。

translations.literal: The established eclipse parts are most detailed and close.
translations.idiomatic: The established eclipse parts are most detailed.

sentences.zh: 其七，古曆二分，晝夜皆等。

translations.literal: Seventh: Ancient calendar at the two equinoxes day and night are equal.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: Ancient calendar at the two equinoxes day and night are equal.

sentences.zh: 胄玄積候，知其有差，春秋二分，晝多夜漏半刻，皆由日行遲疾盈縮使其然也。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan's accumulated observations knew there is difference: at spring and autumn equinoxes day is half a clepsydra mark longer—all because the sun's slow and fast surplus and deficit make it so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan knew there is difference: at spring and autumn equinoxes day is half a clepsydra mark longer—because the sun's slow and fast surplus and deficit make it so.

sentences.zh: 凡此胄玄獨得於心，論者服其精密。

translations.literal: All this Zhouxuan alone grasped in his heart; discussants admired its precision.
translations.idiomatic: All this Zhouxuan alone grasped; discussants admired its precision.

sentences.zh: 大業中卒官。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he died in office.

sentences.zh: 許智藏，高陽人也。

translations.literal: Xu Zhicang Xu Zhicang was a man of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhicang came from Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 祖道幼，嘗以母疾，遂覽醫方，因而究極，世號名醫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daoyou, because his mother was ill, then perused medical formulas and thereby reached the ultimate— the age called him a famed physician.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daoyou, when his mother was ill, studied medical formulas and reached mastery—the age called him a famed physician.

sentences.zh: 誡其諸子曰：「為人子者，嘗膳視藥，不知方術，豈謂孝乎？」

translations.literal: He admonished his sons, saying, "As someone's son, tasting food and inspecting medicine—if one does not know formulas and methods, can it be called filial?"
translations.idiomatic: He admonished his sons, "As a son, tasting food and inspecting medicine—without knowing medicine, can it be filial?"

sentences.zh: 由是世相傳授。

translations.literal: Therefore the craft was transmitted generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the craft passed generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，官至員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He served Liang, reaching the office of Extraordinary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang, reaching Extraordinary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父景，武陵王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Advisory Aide to Prince Wu of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing was Advisory Aide to Prince Wu of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 智藏少以醫術自達，仕陳為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhicang from youth distinguished himself by medical skill and served Chen as Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicang from youth distinguished himself by medicine and served Chen as Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，高祖以為員外散騎侍郎，使詣揚州。

translations.literal: When Chen was destroyed Gaozu made him Extraordinary Regular Attendant and sent him to Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell Gaozu made him Extraordinary Regular Attendant and sent him to Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 會秦孝王俊有疾，上馳召之。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince Xiaogong of Qin was ill; the emperor urgently summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaogong of Qin fell ill; the emperor urgently summoned him.

sentences.zh: 俊夜中夢其亡妃崔氏泣曰：「本來相迎，比聞許智藏將至，其人若到，當必相苦，為之奈何？」

translations.literal: At midnight the prince dreamed his deceased consort Lady Cui weeping, saying, "I came to welcome you, but hearing Xu Zhicang is coming—if that man arrives he will surely torment me; what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the prince dreamed his deceased consort Lady Cui weeping, "I came to welcome you, but Xu Zhicang is coming—if he arrives he will torment me; what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 明夜，俊又夢崔氏曰：「妾得計矣，當入靈府中以避之。」

translations.literal: The next night the prince again dreamed Lady Cui saying, "I have found a plan—I shall enter the spirit office to avoid him."
translations.idiomatic: The next night he dreamed Lady Cui saying, "I have a plan—I shall enter the spirit office to avoid him."

sentences.zh: 及智藏至，為俊診脈，曰：「疾已入心，郎當發巘，不可救也。」

translations.literal: When Zhicang arrived he felt the prince's pulse and said, "The illness has entered the heart; the prince will erupt in rash and cannot be saved."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhicang arrived he felt the pulse and said, "The illness has entered the heart; the prince will erupt in rash and cannot be saved."

sentences.zh: 果如言，俊數日而薨。

translations.literal: It was indeed as he said; the prince died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: It was as he said; the prince died within days.

sentences.zh: 上奇其妙，賚物百段。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his skill and granted a hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and granted a hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，智藏時致仕於家，帝每有所苦，輒令中使就詢訪，或以蒐迎入殿，扶登禦床。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne Zhicang had retired at home; whenever the emperor suffered ailment he would order palace envoys to inquire, or have him searched and brought into the hall, helped up to the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded Zhicang had retired; whenever the emperor suffered ailment envoys inquired, or he was brought to the hall and helped to the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 智藏為方奏之，用無不效。

translations.literal: Zhicang prescribed formulas and submitted them; used, none failed to work.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicang prescribed formulas; used, none failed.

sentences.zh: 年八十，卒於家。

translations.literal: At age eighty he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty he died at home.

sentences.zh: 宗人許澄，亦以醫術顯。

translations.literal: Clansman Xu Cheng also distinguished himself by medical skill.
translations.idiomatic: Clansman Xu Cheng also distinguished himself by medicine.

sentences.zh: 父奭，仕梁太常丞、中軍長史。

translations.literal: His father Shi served Liang as Assistant Director of Ceremonies and Chief Secretary of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi served Liang as Assistant Director of Ceremonies and Chief Secretary of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 隨柳仲禮入長安，與姚僧垣齊名，拜上儀同三司。

translations.literal: Following Liu Zhongli into Chang'an he shared renown with Yao Sengyuan and was appointed Senior Grand Master of State with the Three Excellencies' Honors.
translations.idiomatic: Following Liu Zhongli into Chang'an he shared renown with Yao Sengyuan and was appointed Senior Grand Master of State.

sentences.zh: 澄有學識，傳父業，尤盡其妙。

translations.literal: Cheng had learning and inherited his father's craft, especially reaching its utmost subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had learning and inherited his father's craft, reaching its utmost subtlety.

sentences.zh: 曆尚藥典禦、諫議大夫，封賀川縣伯。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of the Imperial Pharmacy and Director of Ceremonies, enfeoffed as Baron of Hechuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Imperial Pharmacy and Director of Ceremonies, enfeoffed Baron of Hechuan.

sentences.zh: 父子俱以藝術名重于周、隋二代。

translations.literal: Father and son both were famed for craft through Zhou and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both were famed for craft through Zhou and Sui.

sentences.zh: 史失事，故附見雲。

translations.literal: The history lost their affairs, and so they are appended here.
translations.idiomatic: The history lost their affairs, and so they are appended here.

sentences.zh: 萬寶常王令言

translations.literal: Wan Baochang Wang Lingyan
translations.idiomatic: Wan Baochang and Wang Lingyan

sentences.zh: 萬寶常，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Wan Baochang—no one knew where he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Baochang—no one knew his origin.

sentences.zh: 父大通，從梁將王琳歸於齊。

translations.literal: His father Datong followed Liang general Wang Lin in returning to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Datong followed Liang general Wang Lin in returning to Qi.

sentences.zh: 後複謀還江南，事泄，伏誅。

translations.literal: Later he again plotted to return to Jiangnan; the matter leaked and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he plotted to return to Jiangnan; the plot leaked and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 由是寶常被配為樂戶，因而妙達鐘律，遍工八音。

translations.literal: On that account Baochang was assigned as a music household member and thereby mastered pitch and rhythm, skilled in all eight tones.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang was assigned as a music-household member and mastered pitch and rhythm, skilled in all eight tones.

sentences.zh: 造玉磬以獻于齊。

translations.literal: He made jade chime-stones and presented them to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He made jade chime-stones and presented them to Qi.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與人方食，論及聲調。

translations.literal: Once while eating with others he discussed tonal modes.
translations.idiomatic: Once while eating with others he discussed tonal modes.

sentences.zh: 時無樂器，寶常因取前食器及雜物，以箸扣之，品其高下，宮商畢備，諧於絲竹，大為時人所賞。

translations.literal: There being no instruments at hand, Baochang took the dining vessels and miscellaneous objects and struck them with chopsticks, grading their high and low; gong and shang were all complete, harmonizing with strings and bamboo—greatly admired by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: With no instruments at hand he struck dining vessels with chopsticks, grading pitch; gong and shang complete, harmonizing with strings and bamboo—greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 然曆周洎隋，俱不得調。

translations.literal: Yet through Zhou and into Sui he was never given an official post.
translations.idiomatic: Yet through Zhou and Sui he was never given an official post.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，沛國公鄭譯等定樂，初為黃鐘調。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Duke of Pei Zheng Yi and others fixed music, initially as Yellow Bell mode.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaihuang's start Duke of Pei Zheng Yi and others fixed music, initially as Yellow Bell mode.

sentences.zh: 寶常雖為伶人，譯等每召與議，然言多不用。

translations.literal: Though Baochang was a performer, Yi and others often summoned him to discuss—but mostly did not use his words.
translations.idiomatic: Though a performer, Yi often summoned Baochang to discuss—but mostly ignored his words.

sentences.zh: 後譯樂成奏之，上召寶常，問其可不，寶常曰：「此亡國之音，豈陛下之所宜聞！」

translations.literal: Later when Yi's music was complete and submitted, the emperor summoned Baochang and asked whether it would do; Baochang said, "This is the music of a perishing state—how should Your Majesty listen to it!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yi's music was submitted the emperor asked Baochang; he said, "This is the music of a perishing state—how should Your Majesty listen!"

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 寶常因極言樂聲哀怨淫放，非雅正之音，請以水尺為律，以調樂器。

translations.literal: Baochang therefore strongly said the music's sound was grievous, dissolute, and unrestrained—not elegant correct tone—and requested using a water ruler as pitch standard to tune instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang strongly said the music was grievous, dissolute, and unrestrained—not elegant correct tone—and requested a water ruler as pitch standard.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 寶常奉詔，遂造諸樂器，其聲率下鄭譯調二律。

translations.literal: Baochang received the edict and then made all instruments; their sound was uniformly two pitch standards lower than Zheng Yi's tuning.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang received the edict and made all instruments; their sound was uniformly two standards lower than Zheng Yi's tuning.

sentences.zh: 並撰《樂譜》六十四卷，具論八音旋相為宮之法，改弦移柱之變。

translations.literal: He also compiled Music Treatise in sixty-four scrolls, fully discussing the eight tones' rotation as palace method and the changes of shifting strings and moving pillars.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Music Treatise in 64 scrolls, fully discussing eight-tone rotation as palace method and shifting strings and moving pillars.

sentences.zh: 為八十四調，一百四十四律，變化終於一千八百聲。

translations.literal: He made eighty-four modes, one hundred forty-four pitch standards, variations ending at one thousand eight hundred sounds.
translations.idiomatic: He made 84 modes, 144 pitch standards, variations ending at 1,800 sounds.

sentences.zh: 時人以《周禮》有旋宮之義，自漢、魏已來，知音者皆不能通，見寶常特創其事，皆哂之。

translations.literal: People of the time considered that the Rites of Zhou had rotation-as-palace meaning; since Han and Wei, those who knew music could not penetrate it—seeing Baochang specially create this matter, all sneered.
translations.idiomatic: People considered the Rites of Zhou had rotation-as-palace meaning; since Han and Wei music masters could not penetrate it—seeing Baochang create this, all sneered.

sentences.zh: 至是，試令為之，應手成曲，無所凝滯，見者莫不嗟異。
