translations.literal: At this, trial was made to have him do it; at hand it became melody without hesitation—observers all sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Trial was made; at hand melody formed without hesitation—observers sighed in wonder.

sentences.zh: 於是損益樂器，不可勝紀，其聲雅淡，不為時人所好，太常善聲者多排毀之。

translations.literal: He then increased and decreased instruments beyond counting; the sound was elegantly plain—not liked by contemporaries; many in the Grand Temple who knew music disparaged it.
translations.idiomatic: He adjusted countless instruments; the sound was elegantly plain—not liked by contemporaries; Grand Temple music masters disparaged it.

sentences.zh: 又太子洗馬蘇夔以鐘律自命，尤忌寶常。

translations.literal: Also Crown Prince's Librarian Su Kui prided himself on pitch and rhythm and especially resented Baochang.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince's Librarian Su Kui prided himself on pitch and especially resented Baochang.

sentences.zh: 夔父威，方用事，凡言樂者，皆附之而短寶常。

translations.literal: Kui's father Wei was then in power; all who spoke of music attached to him and slighted Baochang.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's father Wei was in power; all who spoke of music attached to him and slighted Baochang.

sentences.zh: 數詣公卿怨望，蘇威因詰寶常，所為何所傳受。

translations.literal: Several times visiting dukes and ministers complaining, Su Wei therefore interrogated Baochang—what he did, from whom he received transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Several times complaining to dukes and ministers, Su Wei interrogated Baochang—from whom he received transmission.

sentences.zh: 有一沙門謂寶常曰：「上雅好符瑞，有言徵祥者，上皆悅之。

translations.literal: A monk told Baochang, "Your Majesty elegantly loves talismanic portents; whoever speaks of auspicious signs the emperor all delights in.
translations.idiomatic: A monk told Baochang, "The emperor loves talismanic portents; whoever speaks auspicious signs delights him.

sentences.zh: 先生當言就胡僧受學，雲是佛家菩薩所傳音律，則上必悅。

translations.literal: My lord should say you received instruction from a foreign monk, saying it is pitch and rhythm transmitted by the Buddhist bodhisattvas—then the emperor will surely be pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Say you received instruction from a foreign monk, saying Buddhist bodhisattvas transmitted the pitch—then the emperor will be pleased.

sentences.zh: 先生所為，可以行矣。」

translations.literal: What my lord does can then be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: What you do can then be carried out."

sentences.zh: 寶常然之，遂如其言以答威。

translations.literal: Baochang agreed and answered Wei exactly thus.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang agreed and answered Wei thus.

sentences.zh: 威怒曰：「胡僧所傳，乃是四夷之樂，非中國所宜行也。」

translations.literal: Wei angrily said, "What the foreign monk transmitted is the music of the four barbarians—not what China should practice."
translations.idiomatic: Wei angrily said, "Foreign monk transmission is barbarian music—not what China should practice."

sentences.zh: 其事竟寢。

translations.literal: The matter in the end was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was shelved.

sentences.zh: 寶常嘗聽太常所奏樂，泫然而泣。

translations.literal: Baochang once heard the Grand Temple's performed music and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang once heard Grand Temple music and wept.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，寶常曰：「樂聲淫厲而哀，天下不久相殺將盡。」

translations.literal: People asked the reason; Baochang said, "The music's sound is dissolute, harsh, and grievous—before long mutual slaughter will nearly exhaust the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "The music is dissolute, harsh, and grievous—before long mutual slaughter will nearly exhaust the realm."

sentences.zh: 時四海全盛，聞其言者皆謂為不然。

translations.literal: At that time the four seas were fully prosperous; those who heard his words all considered it not so.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was fully prosperous; hearers considered it not so.

sentences.zh: 大業之末，其言卒驗。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye his words were finally verified.
translations.idiomatic: At Daye's end his words were verified.

sentences.zh: 寶常貧無子，其妻因其臥疾，遂竊其資物而逃。

translations.literal: Baochang was poor without sons; his wife, while he lay ill, stole his goods and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang was poor without sons; his wife stole his goods and fled while he lay ill.

sentences.zh: 寶常饑餒，無人贍遺，竟餓而死。

translations.literal: Baochang starved with no one to support him and in the end died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang starved unsupported and died of hunger.

sentences.zh: 將死也，取其所著書而焚之，曰：「何用此為？」

translations.literal: About to die he took the books he had written and burned them, saying, "What use is this?"
translations.idiomatic: About to die he burned his books, saying, "What use is this?"

sentences.zh: 見者於火中探得數卷，見行于世，時論哀之。

translations.literal: Observers retrieved several scrolls from the fire; seen circulating in the world—contemporaries mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Observers retrieved several scrolls from the fire; they circulated—contemporaries mourned him.

sentences.zh: 開皇之世，有鄭譯、何妥、盧賁、蘇夔、蕭吉，並討論墳籍，撰著樂書，皆為當世所用。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era Zheng Yi, He Tuo, Lu Ben, Su Kui, and Xiao Ji all discussed tomb classics and compiled music books—all used by the age.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang Zheng Yi, He Tuo, Lu Ben, Su Kui, and Xiao Ji all discussed tomb classics and compiled music books—all used by the age.

sentences.zh: 至於天然識樂，不及寶常遠矣。

translations.literal: As for natural knowledge of music, none approached Baochang remotely.
translations.idiomatic: As for natural knowledge of music, none approached Baochang remotely.

sentences.zh: 安馬駒、曹妙達、王長通、郭令樂等，能造曲，為一時之妙，又習鄭聲，而寶常所為，皆歸於雅。

translations.literal: An Maju, Cao Miaoda, Wang Changtong, Guo Lingyue, and others could compose melodies—a marvel of the age—and also practiced Zheng music; what Baochang made all returned to elegance.
translations.idiomatic: An Maju, Cao Miaoda, Wang Changtong, Guo Lingyue, and others could compose melodies—a marvel of the age—and practiced Zheng music; Baochang's work all returned to elegance.

sentences.zh: 此輩雖公議不附寶常，然皆心服，謂以為神。

translations.literal: These men though in public discussion did not attach to Baochang, yet all in heart submitted, considering him divine.
translations.idiomatic: These men though publicly did not attach to Baochang, yet all in heart submitted, considering him divine.

sentences.zh: 時有樂人王令言，亦妙達音律。

translations.literal: At that time the musician Wang Lingyan also mastered pitch and rhythm with subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Musician Wang Lingyan also mastered pitch and rhythm with subtlety.

sentences.zh: 大業末，煬帝將幸江都，令言之子嘗從，于戶外彈胡琵琶，作翻調《安公子曲》。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye Emperor Yang was about to travel to Jiangdu; Lingyan's son had once followed and outside the door played foreign pipa, performing the variation tune "Lord of Peace Son."
translations.idiomatic: At Daye's end Emperor Yang was about to travel to Jiangdu; Lingyan's son had followed and outside played foreign pipa, performing the variation tune "Lord of Peace Son."

sentences.zh: 令言時臥室中，聞之大驚，蹶然而起曰：「變，變！」

translations.literal: Lingyan was then in his bedchamber; hearing it he was greatly alarmed, started up and said, "Change, change!"
translations.idiomatic: Lingyan was in his bedchamber; hearing it he was alarmed, started up and said, "Change, change!"

sentences.zh: 急呼其子曰：「此曲興自早晚？」

translations.literal: He urgently called his son, saying, "When did this tune arise?"
translations.idiomatic: He urgently called his son, "When did this tune arise?"

sentences.zh: 其子對曰：「頃來有之。」

translations.literal: His son answered, "Just now there was one."
translations.idiomatic: His son answered, "Just now."

sentences.zh: 令言遂歔欷流涕，謂其子曰：「汝慎無從行，帝必不返。」

translations.literal: Lingyan then sobbed and wept, telling his son, "Be careful not to follow on the journey—the emperor will certainly not return."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyan sobbed and told his son, "Do not follow—the emperor will not return."

sentences.zh: 子問其故，令言曰：「此曲宮聲往而不反，宮者君也，吾所以知之。」

translations.literal: The son asked the reason; Lingyan said, "This tune's gong sound goes without returning; gong is the ruler—that is how I know."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Lingyan said, "This tune's gong sound goes without returning; gong is the ruler—that is how I know."

sentences.zh: 帝竟被殺于江都。

translations.literal: The emperor was indeed killed at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was indeed killed at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：陰陽卜祝之事，聖人之教在焉，雖不可以專行，亦不可得而廢也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Yin-yang, divination, and prayer matters—the sages' teaching lies therein; though they cannot be practiced exclusively, they also cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Yin-yang, divination, and prayer—the sages' teaching lies therein; though not to be practiced exclusively, they cannot be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 人能弘道，則博利時俗，行非其義，則咎悔及身，故昔之君子所以戒乎妄作。

translations.literal: If a man can expand the Way, he broadly benefits the customs of the age; if conduct is not according to principle, blame and regret reach the person—therefore the gentlemen of old warned against reckless action.
translations.idiomatic: If a man expands the Way he broadly benefits the age; if conduct violates principle, blame reaches the person—therefore gentlemen of old warned against reckless action.

sentences.zh: 今韋、來之骨法氣色，庾、張之推步盈虛，雖落下、高堂、許負、硃建，不能尚也。

translations.literal: Now Wei and Lai's bone structure and qi-color, Yu and Zhang's calculation of surplus and void—even Luoxia, Gao Tang, Xu Fu, and Zhu Jian cannot surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wei and Lai's bone structure and qi-color, Yu and Zhang's calculation of surplus and void—even Luoxia, Gao Tang, Xu Fu, and Zhu Jian cannot surpass them.

sentences.zh: 伯醜龜策，近知鬼神之情，耿詢渾儀，不差辰象之度，寶常聲律，動應宮商之和，雖不足遠擬古人，皆一時之妙也。

translations.literal: Bochou's tortoise and milfoil nearly knew the spirits' feelings; Geng Xun's armillary sphere did not miss the degrees of celestial signs; Baochang's pitch and rhythm moved in response to gong and shang harmony—though not enough to compare remotely with ancients, all were marvels of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Bochou's divination nearly knew the spirits; Geng Xun's armillary sphere did not miss celestial degrees; Baochang's pitch moved in gong and shang harmony—though not matching ancients remotely, all were marvels of the age.

sentences.zh: 許氏之運針石，世載可稱，蕭吉之言陰陽，近於誣誕矣。

translations.literal: The Xu clan's wielding of needles and stones was famed generation after generation; Xiao Ji's talk of yin-yang approached deceit and absurdity.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu clan's needles and stones were famed generation after generation; Xiao Ji's yin-yang talk approached deceit and absurdity.
